My fave dim sum spot without waiting tooooo long. I find it helpful to take pictures of what I like and show it to the staff to avoid confusing explanations of what you had the last time and "no, not that shrimp, the other one." 

Great food, hands down.
Came here on a busy Sunday. Think waited like 30 mins. Dim sum tasted good and service was pretty good too.

Lake pavilion is one of my go to dimsum places. It's a bit farther away from Main Street and the traffic, and it's relatively more accessible since it's right off the highway. Thy have valet parking though it's almost always packed. The wait time ranges from 10-30 minutes depending on the size of your party. There is always a large variety of food in their carts from rice rolls with fried dough all the way to lobster or stir fried clams. Prices are reasonable and their teas are always fragrant and pair perfectly with the food.

This place has a lot of food. 
I came here during a birthday party & at first I was confused. We had all heard that this would be a buffet - in fact, it was, but in a different way. 
By this, I mean they the buffet came out in courses on our table. Or it could be that this was an event they hosted so the meals came out they way. 
The food came out quickly that we didn't even get to finish the plate. & there were about 15 courses I want to say. The staff was running around & I just want to thank them for keeping their cool the whole time.

This is gritty flushing dim sum.  No pampering service. Getting a seat involved grabbing a number and waiting for a guy to scream your number over the mic.  You may have to share a table with strangers or chase after Dim sum carts.  Expect to be shoved by some patrons without apology and rub elbows   

So why do it.  This is solid authentic dim sum.  Great flavors and prices. There is parking!!!  The waits are fairly reasonable relative to the other flushing spots (30-45 Min at 11 am sunday in November ) . And if you are coming from Long Island like myself, this is logistically the best for the drive. (Main Street exit off the LIE) 

Pro tip.  
Park valet 
Come and get your number 
Sit in car and drink a fine NE IPA.

I've been coming to this restaurant for years mainly for dim sum. Their food has always been average and inconsistent. This was mostly for convenience since we didn't have to venture into the heart of Main Street and they have a parking lot, but the dim sum was never great. Most of the time, the food is room temperature or cold and I swear I was overcharged one time, but couldn't prove it since the stamps they use on the bills don't indicate specific dishes, just size. We only ordered 7-8 items and somehow racked up a bill of $40. Most of the stuff we ordered should've been considered small or medium dishes, but were charged as large and specials. After that, I've only returned once for dinner after they reopened post fire. We ordered the stick rice Dungeness crab since they had a discounted price going for it, but it wasn't good. The crab was dry and not very meaty and it barely had any crab roe (the best part)! If it weren't for convenience, I wouldn't come back if I had a choice.

There is always a line - always!!! The food or service are not very good. The real reason we eat here is because it's walking distance to my grandma's house. Otherwise, I really wouldn't recommend it. If you are dying for dim sum, and you live close by, this place is ok. 

Sometimes the food isn't served hot. 

There's a parking lot but it's chaotic to find a spot because as mentioned, there's a line, always!! 

I'll be back because of Grandma but not by choice.

I always go to the same dim sum place and decided to try something new this time. So, I checked out this place. It's got plenty of tables, wait time was probably about 10 minutes, which is very decent. The dishes were just okay; had better stuff elsewhere. The prices are a little steep; small being $2.95 and there aren't many small dishes to begin with, so you'll be paying for mainly mediums and larges. The baos aren't as soft as they look; cute, but not soft.

Came on Friday noon and got seat easily. 
Maybe it was not too busy. The food we ordered were really good and hot. Egg tart and custard bun were soooo yummy. Only disappointed was the chicken feet was tasteless. It seems like there was some water mixed with the sauce.

We went on Christmas day and we sat after 2 hours of waiting.  I think it's expected during the holidays.  The food was ok, but not enough choices and they were not very hot. They must have been running out of items, because the choices were slim.  The service was outstanding. I would give it another chance on a non holiday.

On Christmas Day, we went to pickup our large takeout order (25-30pp) on the time we were supposed to pickup our order. When we arrived, we were informed by New Lake Pavilion Manager (he used to work inAsian Jewel restaurant in Flushing) that our food wasn't even cooked so we had to wait another 35 mins.  The manager blamed us with the bizarre logic that we should have arrived earlier because they could not produce our order because they were very busy! Apparently this restaurant doesn't need customers, so we will not return to this incompetent and rude restaurant. Almost forgot, a prior large party order we made they forgot to put in 3 dishes in our takeout!

I had a really good experience here at Dim Sum. Since I am not a Dim Sum expert I'll just share a few things I liked:

Since I drive I liked this location - it has a parking lot, but I was able to find a street spot nearby. Going earlier for Dim Sum also helps (before 11am)

Going with a large group allows you to try more dishes, so make some friends and bring them.

I found it very amusing being the only white dude at a table of predominately Asians that nearly all the servers looked directly at me as they spoke Chinese expecting me to understand and answer. This was also funny since I was at a seat furthermost from the carts. Hilarious, I love it!

A friend that frequents Dim Sum spots in Brooklyn/Manhattan more often commented that here there seems to be an abundance of food available where in other spots you practically need to tackle the cart to stop it.

I enjoyed everything I tried from congee, various dumplings, shumai, to the various buns. The extremely fresh egg tarts were fantastic and the silky tofu that you drizzle with ginger simple syrup (honey? but it seemed thinner consistency) was exquisite. Tripe was a bit on chewy side, but not overly so. All very reasonable - surprisingly inexpensive for all I was able to eat.

On a personal note I would like to say my group of dining companions made the whole experience awesome, and a highlight of my holiday season despite the dreary, rainy weather.
Best food ever and deserts delicious service is great so good place for special occasion

Solid place to grab some dim sum! They have authentic dim sum that's well made. Their lobster pan fried noodles are extremely good and it's packed with flavor. They have a variety of buns and their mango pudding wasn't bad either (some pulp which isn't a bad thing). I'm not sure if it was for a limited time but their minion bao's were awesome. They were filled with a yellow custard and black sesame too.

Very very very poor customer service!!!! The waiters were rude and meany when asked for condiments. Food quality was below average. Valet parking was the worst. Overheard the valet guy cursing people in Cantonese when a Mercedes Benz owner gave gratitude that was less than expected. Would NEVER EVER go back again.

This review is for the Dim Sum. The food is spot on; it's flavorful, plentiful, and worth the end bill. There are sooo many carts of foods with a variety of options. Everything tastes fresh since there are so many people that frequent this location. There a few dishes that we always have--I will say that some of their dishes now have fillers (like more rice cake pieces to buffer the ratio of meat). 

Minus 1 star because of the sheer number of people that go. There are lines out the wazoo to this place on the weekends. The wait can easily be upwards of 1.5 hours! The crazy thing is that everyone actually waits. The number of people also increases the responsibility of the servers which are plenty but overwhelming. So don't expect to get the service you'd typically get at restaurants.
The seafood is pretty good. The rest very average. The place is elegant and good for bigger parties.

Had a private room to celebrate a birthday dinner.  The food was delicious, fresh, service was prompt, professional.  Ordered two sushi dishes, not only was it fresh it was presented with a pagoda, beautifully done.  The lobster salad was fresh, not enough for 8 people.  We ordered the conch platter with pea pods, crunchy and tasty, steamed sea bass, Asian broccoli, and vegetables, everything was fabulous.  Lastly we had the red bean sweet soup, the sweet birthday buns and fresh fruit.  Valet parking in the back.  Needed alittle more heat in the restaurant.  Highly recommend the place.

Hmm - it is 3.5 stars.  Nevertheless, given that I will likely be a regular patron going forward, I am giving it a 4 stars.

Need to find a replacement place after Ping closed in Elmhurst.  And this is one of the few places (or maybe the only place) that parking is not a major pain.  Not sure whether it was my lucky day, but found an empty slot at the parking lot.  

As people mentioned, the lines can be long over the weekend.  The food was on-par with other dim-sum places - both in terms of variety and quality.  We had the shrimp shu-mei, har gow, turnip cake, shrimp roll, beef rice roll, and the sticky rice.  The sticky rice was huge ... would have like to see more stuffing but my wife liked it as it was.

Service was good - the waiter even exchanged our plates with clean ones which is unusual in Chinese dim sum places.

If you want to avoid the crowded congestion of Flushing and have a car, this is a great place to go to.  It has a small parking lot which gets filled up pretty quickly during the busy hours and street parking, which can be easy or a pain.  There is a bus route that goes there too (~20-25 mins).

Better to go with a group so can try more dishes.  I got there early so got a table while waiting for friends trying dim sum for the first time.  It took a while for my friends to find street parking since the parking lot was full.  I ordered the basics (ie shrimp dumplings, short ribs, sui mai (meat with shrimp dumplings)) until another friend joined us.  My friends tried and liked the chicken feet and intestines which I was surprised.

They are willing to try more next time.

We stumbled upon Lake Pavilion looking for a Chinese eatery. We were visiting from Montreal. The waiting was well worth it. We had among many other dishes, bamboo wrapped steam rice, tripes and durian rolls, etc. During our seven day New York stay, we returned three times. The service was prompt for return tea. The food came by so often and so tempting that we had to  refuse it( belly space limited!). At the end, we took leftovers home and had snacks for the rest of the day. The experience was very courteous and did not break the bank!
Their dim-sum are very good. I had tried same type of dim-sum in some other places, but they have better taste! I like their bamboo roll, which has both meat and vege style

Given the fact that today's Lunar / Chinese new year day, with lots of people waiting for seats, the servers did a good job! It was still about 45 mins wait but once we sat, all the foods are worth it. 

One of the new items is the durian pancake. Durian is not for everyone but I am one of those who love it. The pancake was warm and crispy on the outside and creamy durian filling on the inside. 

The shrimp wrapped with rice flat noodle is one of my favorites at dimsum. My family and I ate a lot more than these photos. I was busy eating and forgot to take pictures as we get each dish. Dimsum is always with lots of options to choose from as the workers push carts around.

Most unprofessional restaurant ever. They messed up our menu order during a family event between two tables. As a resolution, the waitress just took the dishes from the kids table which were half eaten and swapped it with our table. Ultimately we just got half eaten food and they blamed the kids for eating it.

Manager did absolutely nothing. So unprofessional. Did not own up to anything or offer anything for the half eaten food.
Decent Chinese food. Large space if that's you style fast service no frills. Good dim sum.

Went here with some friends/co-workers. Got a private room and it was a really nice experience. Some of my fave dishes were:
Peking Duck w/ Dough
Prawns w Walnuts (highly suggested)
Steak w Asparagus (very flavorful)
Pan Fried Noodles
Overall a really nice experience w some great people. Would definitely recommend going and experiencing.
Unreliable service, rude staff. Avoid this place at all costs. Food finally came after 1.5 hrs of wait, no apology. Nothing.

Always packed for lunch, but since there are more tables than you can count, it moves fast. I would actually be quite worried if a dimsum place wasn't packed, so it comes with the territory. 

They serve all the dimsum classics and its better than most places in NYC. The move is to just ask for the menu if you aren't feeling the love with the pace of the food coming out on carts or want something else, the kitchen is massive and they can cook whatever you are looking for. 

Its a super-local crowd and cantonese/mandarin is spoken more than english, but if you don't know what to order, just look around, point, getup and peak into the carts and just enjoy yourself. 

The parking lot is inadequate, so don't try to park close to it unless you just hit the lotto and feel like its your lucky day. Nice spot outside of the crazy main st. area of flushing

For Pete's sake ... do not come here during the peak hours on weekends .. 11:30 am to 1:30 pm - unless you are prepared to wait 30 to 45 minutes for a table. Larger parties get seating preference, parties less than 4 may be asked to share a table.

Loud, kid friendly place with many dialects of Chinese spoken ...

The quality of the dim sum is very good and come out fast, service is fast & efficient.

Big plus is that they have their own parking lot.
Great experience from beginning to end.  Valet parking attentive service classic authentic food .  Can't miss.

Well I never had a meal of dim sum, but I can go with it! The hub brought home some dumplings from this very large restaurant. It used to be a diner many years ago. So we shared shrimp dumplings very good! Pork dumplings my least favorite. I wouldn't reorder and the shrimp in rice noodles. I liked these a lot. I would go back just to see what else they have to order. I will most definitely check out more dim sum spots so stay tuned! I ate them and forgot to take a pic!

Came out to this restaurant for my grandfathers 80th birthday.  As much as me and my family enjoyed the food, the cons just overwhelm me from giving this place a great review.  First off, I didn't think it would be so hard for me to find a server to take a birthday cake and candles to the back. One after another they would just stare and say they would come back. One waiter would just shout at me telling me to give it to my server.  Well If I knew who my server was I sure wouldn't have had that problem.  Another issue, was that my grandmother kept on calling them trying to get their attention so we can get things for the table.  They would just walk right past you like you don't exist.  It is only until I literally had to raise the tone of my voice,did they even acknowledge me.   I know this place has the reputation of making great food.  However, unless my family makes specific requests for this place, I probably won't be making the trip all the way out there for it.

The food here was good, not great. We came in on a Saturday afternoon between lunch and dinner time. The place itself was a little dingy, the service quick but not overly friendly. We ordered the veggie and shrimp steamed dumplings as well as a chicken w mixed vegetables. They give you some peanuts to snack on while you wait for your food and there's a parking lot, which is a plus. All in all, a decent but unremarkable meal.

Last night we were stuck on the LIE out to Long Island and decided rather than sit in traffic for another hour, get off at Flushing Main Street and look for a place to eat.  We have seen New Lake Pavilion from the roadway many times, so we decided to take a chance even though it looks a bit garish.  It reminds me a lot of restaurants in Hong Kong, that are large, busy, but great food.  We weren't wrong.  The dim sum was great and the pork and chicken dishes we had were excellent....and huge portions.  Great find.

This place is usually known for their dimsum but this day was for family style eating. The dishes itself had very basic flavors, just like how most Asian restaurants that do this style would taste. None of their dishes really stood out to me like wow this is what makes this place better than the other restaurant. Service was good since they replaced plates every so often where the plates looked like they needed space. Overall very mediocre for a family style but I would come back for dim sum next time.

Came here on MDW for lunch. What's better than having dim sum for lunch? 

Don't look for fancy decor, friendly staff, or ambiance. You get none of that. It looks a bit old and old school inside. The wait staff are just busy working, they don't check on you after they seated you. You have to flag them down if you need anything - so don't be shy. 

The dim sum staff are walking around with all different kinds of dim sum. They sometimes push what they have to you if you aren't interested feel free to let them know. Don't be shy. They will go away. It's a dim sum restaurant everyone's talking and having a good family time. That means it's loud, it's especially loud during rush hours. Oh don't be surprised that you may have to share a table with others when they get busy. It's also a very common practice. 

Make sure you know what kind of tea you like to be drinking when you are having dim sum. Because that's the first question the wait staff will ask you. I usually go for chrysanthemums, oolong, Tieguanyin, puerh or anything you fancy. Note don't expect the quality of the tea is top notched because they just aren't. You can have just water too. 

I would go for the shrimp dumplings (har gow) and shrimp rice rolls (cheung fun) - yum yum yum
I like their egg tarts, molten custard buns, mango mochi or durian mochi. I am a happy camper once I have tried them all. Their meat dishes are very good too. Ribs, rice dumpling with chicken, bbq pork buns, beef balls, chicken feet, beef tripes, sui mai, and all the traditional or non-traditional dim sum dishes. 


Overall, it's a pretty decent dim sum place. The price is reasonable too. :)
Had dim sum last Sunday with my family and it was packed. The food was really good and friendly staff. I really enjoyed it. Will come here again !

Been here many times for both dim sum and dinner. I prefer having dinner over their dim sum. Service varies. If it's a good day, you'll get friendly service. If it's a crappy day, you might have to hail for a waiter multiple times before you give them the death stare. 

Recently had the dungeness crab stir fried with black bean sauce over ho fun. The ho fun was delicious! The snails were also good! And no, it's not the type of snails that you find sliming around in your backyard. Edible snails for food consumption purposes. It's sort of like the mini version of escargot but tastier and less fatty since its not soaked in some herb butter. Most of their seafood dishes are pretty good. If you have no idea of what to order, their menu has pictures! The restaurant is huge so they can easily accommodate big parties!

As far as Dim Sum goes, terrible service, extremely rude staff. Asked for a dish and it never came. If you have to go around and find your own dishes, it might as well be a buffet. Also there's no parking on Sunday's around the area and the valet lot is usually full. If you're looking for a dim sum suggestion, my best advice is to not come here

Had a family gathering on a Sunday afternoon in one of the party rooms. We had 12 people eating a combination of dim sum and regular menu dishes. We ordered several things like fried noodles, fried rice, a vegetable dish, and a whole roasted duck. Besides that we were planning on getting lots of dim sum stuff. They said the carts would come but only a few did and it was never what we wanted. Every once in a while this lady would come in the room and look around meanly. We would ask for food and she would say "later." After some time, a couple of us went to the front where they sell dim sum to go. They bought a bunch of food and brought it back to us and we ate the take out food in the party room. Some of our food never came but was on our bill, like the fried rice, and our whole duck was a half duck, and we had 5 plates of soup dumplings but were billed for 6. They said we ate the food and have to pay. When it's a large group, review the bill, and watch the stamping. They def take advantage of a big group losing track of what they ate. Parking situation is bad.

I've started coming here after a recent near-fraud experience happened at another dim sum restaurant that I went to. I've been here before but I chose this as my staple because the food and service been really great.

You can't miss it on the road, it really looks like a pavilion but don't try looking for a lake.

But you'll definitely want to find parking because on certain days, you wont have any luck getting into valet. Most of the area is residential so at least that part is free. If you do park at the valet, you'll have to leave your keys and it's also free but tip should be given. 

I've mostly came for the dim sum which is great and I don't think it's really expensive. You'll still be able to get even after 12pm. Once you get to ordering, the dim sum carts will start moving in on you to try to get you to buy their plates. They're not forceful about it and really polite. I appreciate that they have variety of rice rolls here whereas other restaurants only have the shrimp and beef kind. The food is always warm because when they get it, they get it from near the bottom of the pile.

Service is also great. They almost always got you when your teapot is near empty or you're done with a plate. This place hasn't given me a reason not to be my staple.

The food used to be better here before the fire.  Now, going with friends that's say this is the best, even though this is their first time here, the food and especially the service sucks.  The dinner here is okay, charging high prices for subpar food.  The dim sum here was half the quality of our favorite Cantonese food, even though every dish is hot.  The chicken lo mein was just boiled frozen egg noodles you buy from the store, drowned in some sauce with some old Chinese broccoli and so little chicken.  The beef noodle soup was the same too, except with lots of bland soup broth and very little beef.  However, I was critical of the service given here.  One of the servers here was very snooty, as we have to ask her for other items, while giving a bad attitude to the nine of us.  If I had to introduce somebody to dim sum or to Cantonese food, I would go somewhere else, even if it is more expensive.

The food was alright.
We got:
-Har Gow (steamed shrimp dumplings): 
-Pai Gwut (Steamed Pork Ribs)
-Fong Djau (Steamed Chicken Feet)
-Nor Mai Gai (Sticky Rice in Lotus Leaves)
-Mah Lai Goh (Sponge Cake)
-Salted Egg Custard Bun
-Zhenzhu Qui (steamed pearl balls - meat ball inside sticky rice)
-Fried fish with green pepper 
-Vegetable watercress dumpling
The custard buns and sponge cake were good. The pork ribs were okay. Everything else was eh.

We came here for dinner on a Friday evening and the place wasn't too packed. The lobster ginger & scallion; chicken & broccoli and general sos (best my son said he had as a Chinese food foodie). Service was also good! Next time will try the dim sum. Family portion style was more than enough!

Food is pretty good here. I've came here many times and tasted all of the most expensive dishes. Service is good here besides dim sum. When it's morning or afternoon at dim sum hour it's very packed and sometimes waiter can be rude because of overcrowding. They have private rooms here where you can eat and sing karaoke. You can also bring your own liquor and have a blast.

Usually come here on the weekend for Dim Sum, but we wanted to try the night scene for the first time. They had some specials for the night and we had the house special steak with red wine sauce, fried tofu with conch and winter melon with seafood soup. Food was tasteful and we were in an out in less than an hour. We got our food items with 5 - 10 minutes from the time we ordered. Efficient!

Worst establishment ever. Waiters do not speak a drop of English and cannot explain the menu items. Condiments are scarce. I asked for a Pepsi and the waiter said "pepper?" As he pointed to a bottle of soy sauce on the table. We were Charged for food we never received. Their "Vegetarian" options were full of meats so vegetarians can't even eat here. Service was horrible and they wrote down our orders on the guest check in Chinese and left it on the table the entire time. We were supposed to get noodles with our order- that never came so we had to order it separately. We could barely understand the writing when the bill was summed and couldn't make sense of an extra 10$ so we left and even left tip then they ran us down while we were leaving and magically spoke English now asking us to leave a tip because tip wasn't included on the bill. So we gave them some money and left. The food is NOTHING special and was not worth the price tag. You are better off ordering from your local Chinese place, this one was a huge disappointment in service and taste.

Excellent flavorful food, always consistent with good service. Attractive but noisy. However, you go there to eat, not to wine and dine and have intimate conversation. Food is always attractively displayed and consistently tasty. No MSG and they will make dishes for you on request. Don't miss out on the jellyfish platter and the Mayonnaise shrimp. Make sure you make reservations or prepare for a bit of a wait - this restaurant gets crowded on the weekend. Best Chinese food I have had outside of Chinatown.

Food was better before the fire. Not only myself feels this way but my family too. I guess the chefs must have left during closure for many months. Used to be packed but now so empty during dinner time. 

Dinner are so overpriced when u compare with the better taste before.

This place is great. With a massive exception. I go with my family about once a week or so. A woman who takes the bil ALWAYS DEMANDS more of a tip.
Considering my family has been going there for years. I think i need to find another place to eat.

This place always is packed to wait from half hour to longer. The service is so so and the varieties of dimsum is good.  The parking is the worst even if they have a parking lot it is always filled. To expect a spot you have to drive around and around. I go here is because my family lives in queens. You have to he here early like 11am. Otherwise I prefer not to get into this hassle just to eat. We on Long Island have couple of places just as good.
Terrible and rude staff.   Ingredients are sketchy and therefore the food isn't fresh/good tasting.  Parking lot is a nightmare.  Look elsewhere for dim sum in NY.

New Lake Pavilion is a Cantonese dim sum restaurant located near the junction of Flushing's Main Street and the Long Island Expressway. We tried coming over once before but was thwarted by the lack of parking in the restaurant's lot and on the street. Given this situation, we came a little earlier and was fortunate to find parking through the valet in the lot. The parking is all valet, so be prepared to cough up a couple of bucks, but it was worth it. 

The restaurant itself is a stand-alone building with one large rectangular dining room, although there are some private rooms set aside near the entrance. The restaurant décor had a European flavor to it with hanging chandeliers and was brightly lit with big windows alongside one wall of the dining room. We got a number and was seated in a round five-seat table. I saw many tables of varying sizes. We were there on a Sunday morning at 10:30, and it took about 20 minutes to get seated.

As for the dim sum, I must say that their food is a major revelation. I've never seen dim sum created in such majestic sizes as I did here. I would say about 30 percent of the dim sum was either larger or had a special twist to it that set it aside from other restaurants. For example, we ate siu mai which had an entire shrimp embedded on top of the pork. The shrimp size was equally impressive in the cheong fun. The eggplant stuffed with shrimp was gigantic and it took more than ten bites to finish a single one off. Another abnormally sized item was the bacon wrapped shrimp. We also tried the ginger tofu, herbal chicken feet, sticky rice, beef cheong fun (which was really beefy - with less fat) and cha siu bao with a pineapple bun top! 

This was my first visit but it was memorable for what the owners attempted to do, which is to differentiate the dim sum. I felt their goal was accomplished and I will come back as often as I can!

Just had our wedding here last weekend and our guests had a great time. Everyone raved about the food (I kept hearing about the lobster, Peking duck, and desserts). They helped put up a partition (which was beautiful) in the main dining room, which gave us more privacy to hold a ceremony since we didn't fill up the whole main area. We had to do a lot of legwork to figure out the menu and discuss with the manager, especially with 2 different menus, but everything worked out!

Been here for Banquet a few times. Foods are quite good. After this dinner with just two of us. I come to the conclusion that the food here is good for large group, because the portion is big and it's good value for the price.
Steam fish was cook perfectly, but the good meal ends there for me. MSG gives me headaches.The tofu with mushrooms, stirred fired rice noodles and soup where all prepared with heavy amount of MSG. If that's not an issue for you, come and enjoy a good value meal.
Service was very friendly and good.
Very crowded, waited an hour for a table. Crab with sweet rice delicious. Taisun sweet dumpling yum yum

Came here with someone who knew the menu... thankfully. I don't think I would have known what to order as the menu is very traditional (or at least way more traditional than I've experienced).
We ended up ordering the following
- Steamed shrimp dumplings - VERY fresh tasting
- Peking Duck which was sliced table side and placed into steamed buns
- Fried seabass with sauce on the side.  The waiter brought the live fish to our table before preparing.
- Seafood pan fried noodles - very fresh seafood.  The noodles were very crisp

There were many "interesting" looking dishes being delivered to other tables around us.  I wasn't really sure what many of them  were.  Service was friendly, but communication was a little difficult with some of the waitstaff.
The decor is also pretty interesting to say the least.

Great food with a lot of choices, ok service, but as other reviews said they hassle for tips. The lady at the cashier told the host that we tipped "low" Why tell the host?

Not coming again. We have other spots in town we go often and never have we gotten this much rudeness over tipping. Not even for dim sum but in general for flushing/chinatown/elmhurst restaurants. If you're struggling for cash then please raise the prices instead of taking out on customers who come out to eat at your establishment.

More like 3.5 stars for the dim sum portion only. They have an extensive dinner menu which I haven't tried yet.
We went on a Monday afternoon thinking it wouldn't be as busy as weekends but nope, it seems lunchtime dim sum will be hectic any day of the week. There is free valet parking on the 60th Avenue side (but do tip them). We had to wait a bit for the valet but not long (just have one of your party run into the restaurant and get a number to queue up for a table while you wait ). Be forewarned, do not try to jump queue in the parking lot as we witnessed someone try to do. The attendant will shoo you off with a body gesture just short of a middle finger and a fongool fist.
The cramped waiting area in the restaurant with the flux of patrons coming and going felt like I was in the middle of the Game Of Thrones Battle of the Bastards scene but we were eventually seated in perhaps 10-15 minutes (typical). The dim sum is pretty standard. Rice noodles, chicken feet, egg rolls and more. The waiters/waitresses pop in frequently like Whack-a-mole to collect your empty plates but did not refill our tea pot though.
We ordered plenty for our party of 3 people (around a $70 bill: don't judge) because we have a tendency to eat as if we hadn't been fed in weeks. I have no explanation for this so I'll just blame my perimenopause. It must have been around 14 dishes so it's an average price of $5 per dish (again, don't judge our healthy appetites. We did have about 4 or so take-home containers for the items we could not finish)
With standard dim sum fare, I think the Minion buns (with black sesame/egg custard filling) is a draw. They are adorable. We got the aged minion with the wrinkly forehead and gummy lips, as if the poor fella didn't put his dentures in (photo evidence attached). The standout here for me (and my tummy) is they have the almond tofu dessert which I can't seem to find in other dim sum spots and it's delicious. Richer in texture and very creamy as if there's less gelatin and more tofu.
I would definitely return just to get the almond tofu dessert, which I can just grab from the take-out area on the Main Street entrance (or just find street parking), or for a sit-down for that always special dim sum experience (I swear, it's like a sport. At times you're in and out of your seat chasing those food carts down). As for other take-out dim sum, I'll stick with Good Fortune supermarket on Queens Boulevard, which has a less hectic parking lot and doesn't feel like I'm fighting in Battle of the Bastards for my dish of shrimp noodles.

Came here for dinner on Tuesday with my family. First of all the staff is extremely rude here. A waitress said "move, move, move" to one of us instead of asking nicely to excuse her. Then we ordered a round of beer and we asked for a glass and she said only wine glasses and suggested my brother in law to just drink it out of the bottle instead if he didn't want to use the wine glasses. Rude rude rude!!!! No one asked her for her opinion.

 First dish comes in and we asked the waitress to please serve us, because it was a big platter of appetizers and she said " her back would break if she had to serve each of us"...umm it's ur job duh!! She wasn't happy to do it, so we told her forget it. Throughout the whole dinner, the waitresses that served us wasn't attentive at all. And it was NOT busy at all. There was only 4 other tables.

Supposedly the restaurant was renovated not long ago, but it felt dirty and grimy. The floors was so slippery and nasty that I had to used Lysol wipes to clean my 19 months old child shoes before I got home. And the worst part, our child got a high fever later that night and the doctor confirmed two days later he got Coxsackie virus.  Lastly we smelled cigarette smoke throughout our dinner and couldn't understand where it was coming from since we booked a VIP  room for dinner but soon we learned why. This restaurant allow guests to smoke inside the restaurant. As we were leaving the VIP room a guy walked by me INSIDE the restaurant smoking a cigarette and no one stopped him and he entered the VIP room next to us. 

I went home pissed because after all this crap listed above, the food was below average. Never going back and I will not suggest this place to anyone. Go somewhere else, there are plenty of better restaurants in the heart of Flushing, Queens.

Had a great dim sum experience with my mom and toddler. We loved the tripe, and a lot of try dim sum we got was steamed. Delicious and light! We were seated right away and it was bustling with so many options. It's convenient because it's right off the LIE.

Just raced home from New Lake Pavilion in Flushing. Apparently, when they translated the menu, they left the word "fish" out, instead replacing it with "shrimp." Well, guess which one I'm allergic to... In addition to it being VERY greasy, I've now apparently eaten enough fish sauce to spend most of the evening in the bathroom. When we questioned the waiter, he spoke no English. Oh, and the bathroom was DISGUSTING, turds floating in unflushed toilets. The place was empty. I should've known better.

Good place to bring large groups on Chinese New Year or for family reunions. The menu is quite expansive and the dishes are very good and authentic, if a bit pricy. The most memorable dish I had here was the miniature red octopuses.
Authentic Chinese food. Great spot for dim sum. Always packed but wait times are not bad. Huge dining room with many tables.

This might be my new favorite dim sum spot. It isn't at the heart of Flushing, but there's parking in the back. The managers and dim sum cart ladies are all super friendly here. The space is huge. I've even had a friend host his wedding here. There are large windows and clean chairs with decorated seat covers.

Even on very quiet weekdays, this place has all of the dim sum dishes I like. If you want fresh bakery foods, just go to the front. Their deliciously fluffy egg tarts don't come out until around 10:30/11am. I really like their steamed rice wrapped in the lotus leaf here. Their rice rolls are mediocre. It doesn't wrap all the way around. I would get their various steamed dumplings, beef tendons, shumai, pastries, and buns. The shumai here has shrimp. There is no option without it. I brought a friend here who doesn't eat seafood and wanted to show her all the basic dim sum dishes, so I got shumai. To my surprise, all of the shumai had shrimp in them and it sounds as a large order, so just beware of that. They make an excellent coconut pudding and tofu-fa (pudding) as well. Weekdays are less crazy, but on weekends, there are all the great food options since there are more people. Fresher foods rotate out faster since there's a higher demand. This restaurant also has all the traditional dinner items and tons of alcohol for your large family gatherings. 

There's a bakery area out front where you can also get the 3 dishes over rice combo. The bakery has all of the Chinese bread essentials. I also have to highlight how delicious their egg tarts are here. Definitely try that! There's also roast pork, roast duck, soy sauce chicken, duck wings, and scallion chicken out front as well. Grab some food to go!

Beware: I've come here on rainy days. The area near where you pay/ramp/bathroom are extremely extremely slippery! Hold on to whatever you can to make sure you don't slip. Definitely help your elderly family members. I went flying in rain boots. Worth the slip and slide for this nice food though.

This rating is only for grabbing DimSum to-go! 

We grabbed some dim sum to go to visit some friends and everything was pretty good. Total spent was around 20 dollars for 5 items and 4 chashu baos. 

We actually ordered a few more items but they forgot it to add it. We weren't charged for it so it was fine.

The food came out quickly and was packed well. They were busy but we got our food in a timely matter.

Overall would recommend getting DimSum to go here! Maybe will get a chance to dine in some other time.

Food is ok.. nothing screamed out to me besides the amount of salt! There are better options in this class of restaurants, but it is appealing because they have parking!!! The restaurant gets quite busy during the weekend so you end up yelling across the table in order to be heard. Their parking lot was also full right before I was about to pull in.

THE GOOD:
The melon shrimp mushroom soup was really yummy and comes in the melon itself. You wouldn't be able to make this at home so it is worth it HOWEVER it was sooo salty.
The razor clams tasted good and you will love it if you love jalapeños. HOWEVER my mom didn't like it because she said she bit into a lot of sand, meaning they didn't clean it well enough.

THE BAD:
Their tofu with scallops had "XO" sauce which tasted oyster-y and spicy - it was weird, I didn't like it. 
The fried mini fishies were not crunchy and tasted like it was sitting out for 15 minutes. 
The water vegetables had a nice texture but soo salty.
I don't even know what the other dishes in my pictures were- they just did not taste good at all. Especially the thing with shiitake mushrooms in the clay pot- it is supposed to be fish but I have no idea what I ate. It had the texture of pork
Excellent. Fun and the food was constantly circulating. I found it by accident but it will now be my go to location

Weekends are like chaos even around 10am. Be prepared to wait a bit and not have an estimate when you will be seated (they have big and small tables so giving an estimated time is a bit difficult). Despite all this, the dim sum food comes out fresh and very regularly so there is not a dead portion of time. The food quality is pretty good and they have specialty foods too that other dim sum restaurants do not have. Overall it's cheap and good for big gatherings. Don't expect a quiet atmosphere. They do have a parking lot but it is pretty packed. You could find street parking nearby with a little bit of effort. Overall, good dim sum with lots of food carts being pushed and family environment.

Parking attendants didn't like their tip so engaged the customer in a verbal fight. Waving of fingers in face, the usual idiotic violent behavior of sub-human racists - racist because they said they customer was rude because they were Korean. Yelled at the customer in Cantonese too. 

When someone started to film them, they got all quiet for a minute - wonder why. They started up again soon after, this time in Chinese.

So not to be racist myself, but I've never seen attendants of any other ethnicities yell at a customer for not leaving the tip they is "required." 

I mean, the food here is ooookay and the service is hit or miss as it is. Also think they charge more if you don't speak Chinese. I order the some things elsewhere and they are priced differently. Here it's all priced at "large"

Well, it's not it's the only dimsum place...
Crazy busy here on Sundays for lunch dim sum, choices are plentiful, parking is always a nightmare issue around 2 blocks area.

Me and my boyfriend came here for some dim sum we both like su mai and shrimp rolls and we came to basically eat that , I was really looking forward to having su mai and frankly when the ladies come to us with the food truck they are quick to leave. Every time I asked if they had su mai they said later not now. So while we were eating other things two people sat down next to us and they were quick to get su mai. Now I mentioned o wanted su mai at least 5 times to her and she never brought me it. But was quick to give it to the people near us. The place needs to be more organized it's kinda like a in and out service it's to fast they need to slow down a little and get more English speaking people working. This is America the native language is English. So you will have English speaking ppl at these types of places and it's difficult to understand them when they don't know English.

Went in to Lake Pavilion with friends today. It was quite a busy time, and it was quite a struggle to get trolleys to stop by. I'm not sure if this was just that the weren't many going around or if it was our placement in the restaurant, but it was difficult to get service.
The food was mediocre, not superb, but not bad either. 
Stop in if you're passing by, but don't go too out of your way.

Whenever my family has banquets or big celebrations, we usually have it at Lake Pavilion. This is the right place to go to if you're looking for traditional Cantonese styled food. The portion sizes are HUGE and definitely meant for sharing with everyone at the table. My family's go to favorites are the Peking duck, mayonnaise shrimp served with walnuts and broccoli, and the sweet and sour pork. This place also serves dim sum in the mornings/afternoons and it's usually very crowded.

The great thing about this place is that they also have private rooms with 1-2 tables depending on how big your party size is!

Whenever I'm spending the weekend at my friend's place in Queens, we always make sure to get dim sum at New Lake Pavilion because #tradition and also because the dim sum here is actually pretty dang good. Over the years, we've eaten our way through many, many dim sum spots throughout Flushing and we all agree that New Lake Pavilion will always be our main. 

Not only is it super convenient to get to because there actually is a parking lot, their dim sum is tasty and there is of course a huge variety to choose from. We always get the classics--Shrimp Dumplings, Pork Ribs, Sticky Rice in Lotus Leaves, Shrimp Noodle Rolls--and all-time my favorite... the Chinese Donut Noodle Rolls, which I only seem to be able to get here! 

While the service is a bit lacking (which dim sum place isn't though?), the food more than makes up for it. Can't wait to continue this tradition until we're 135!
Great dim sum and a great experience with friend or family. Honestly if you're adventurous, try anything

I have been to Lake Pavilion a few times over the past few years but this weekend, I had the luxury to have it twice! Dim sum and Cantonese-style cuisine is amazing here! I spent last weekend here for dim sum with friends and to celebrate my grandma's birthday over dinner. Both experiences were great! 

For dim sum, Baked Pork Buns, any Cheung Fun (Rice Rolls), and Tofu Dessert are the best! Baked Pork Buns were so flavorful so get it while its hot! Cheung Fun is so soft and fresh, loved it! Tofu Dessert, come on, you can't leave dim sum without this delicious bowl of sweetness. During dim sum, the cart ladies can be aggressive in trying to sell you expensive, not-so-good items, don't be afraid to say no, if you don't want it. 

For dinner, everything was almost perfect. My favorite had to be the Dungeness Crab with Steamed Rice. This was so flavorful and the rice was so soft! I loved it! 

Valet parking makes it easy for everyone to meet up too.

I am baffled by the ratings of this place on Yelp, this is THE place if you want authentic Chinese banquet style food, especially Cantonese seafood.  It is always packed, uniformly by Chinese households having family celebrations or get-togethers: the grandparents insisting on coming here, the parents ordering crabs the size of ceiling fans, and the grandkids who would rather be with their friends at a more trendy place are probably the ones leaving reviews.

Of course, the standard practices at all Chinese restaurants exist here.  The prices on the menu and the prices on your bill don't always match.  Be prepared to pay when you order any live seafood by the pound, so don't be surprised when that minuscule live fish you ordered turned out to be a whale price-wise.  

Other than that, the food is consistently good and service efficient.  The menu is enormous, and all the classic dishes are available, in different versions, and all done well.  You will see exotic seafood options here not available elsewhere that only a marine biologist would recognize.  Honestly the special menu reads like a pamphlet at an aquarium.  

Don't bother coming here unless you have more than 5 in your party, unless it's for dim sum, otherwise you won't make a dent on the menu.  And another tip, let the attendants play Tetris with your car in the small lot in the back, I am convinced every house in the neighborhood has at least three driveways each.

The worst takeout service ever !!!  this is not the first time it happened . Just because of the holiday doesn't mean you can just hang around and play with food containers . customer standing on line over 30 minutes-because no one is taking order . For example , she took  my order , Instead of packed  and tell me what  I am owe , so I can pay . I waited it another 10 minute watch her  open empty container packet and stacking on the table . When I complain to the cashier.  why is she stacking plastic container instead of pack my food . She screamed at me and tell me , can you  see she's busy. This is not how you run a Business . Many people on line also was upset . I definitely not good  way for service industry

Big banquet hall dim sum/ Chinese restaurant. Dim sum very good. Chinese food pretty good. They have many private rooms for family dinners. Employees could be friendlier. Valet parking. Can get very busy and have a wait during peak times. Popular restaurant among many Chinese friends and families. Obviously I'll be back.

Finally made it here and have to say the food was all delicious. But food is just one part of the experience. The hostess was very nice and friendly seated us right away. We had dinner for 2 New Year's Day and it wasn't as busy but it could be because it was an early dinner. As we left it got more busy. Aside from someone bringing us a steaming towel to wipe our hands and a drink order as soon as we were seated, no one came up to take our order for a long time. I had trouble getting someone's attention to ask a question and when I did they seemed bothered. I asked the price of dish listed as market price so there's no obvious answer there, not sure why he was annoyed. When we finally did order, one item (the bbq spare ribs) wasn't available. Waiter wasn't remotely apologist and just stoic waiting for us to name a back up item as if we planned for that. We put in the order for the rest of the items and asked for some time. We eventually were ready but again had trouble getting someone's attention. Mind you the place was 1/4 full. We asked for a sauce with the dumplings and the waiter gave us a rude stare and said there's no sauce. We said is there any kind of sauce that maybe comes with other dishes even a soy sauce? Once again he seemed annoyed, but went to get it anyway. Back to the food. Everything was cooked well, the sizzling beef could have came with another vegetable not just onion and peppers and was bit gooey but enjoyable. The steamed shrimp dumplings may just be the best I ever had. The quality and chunk of shrimp was amazing I can possibly eat 10 as a meal. The crispy garlic chicken was SO good. Everything was plated aesthetically which is important to foodies like me. Everything is pricey. Like super pricey. For the service and over priced menu it lost 2 stars. Hard to say if I'll be back but those shrimp dumplings may just make me have to.

Dimsum place open start from 9:30 but you better be there 10 min early so you can get a table ready or be ready to wait 20-30 min. They are full house. 

Dimsum here does taste fresh and i bet they are made from scratch. A lot of dishes to choose from from steam, fry, desserts... expect to try on different dishes you dont see all the time from other dimsum restaurant (drooling). 

Highlight of the day: steam egg custard - when you open the bun, a golden egg lava coming out and you have to close your eyes when eating it because it SO DAMN GOOD 

Please try the Steam Egg Custard and you know what im talking about

PARKING: easy parking on st, weekday and sat pay $2 for 1hr and they have Valet parking lot (tip $2) so basically the same thing. Dont have to worry about finding parking spot

The Dim Sum is ok, but the dinner is just average. 
They have a parking lot, but normally will be full on weekend. People waiting to get in the lot and cars even blocking the road.
There is a take-out place on the side for bread, dim sum, Cantonese BBQ meats and lunch special (three choices & soup).
I like their bread, and even better after 6 pm for buy 1 get 1 free.

Get out of here with this place. 
First of all, we walked in, the place was half under water. I guess there was a leak in the bathroom that flooded out into the front of the restaurant.
But honestly, not even gonna hold that against them. Issues arise.
But we ordered, I went second. The waiter told me NO. The waiter said no to what I ordered. He said the dish the first person ordered was family style so we should share. And then showed me some vegetable dish and said, "get this."
Also, some of the shrimp in the shrimp dumpling wasn't fully cooked. Which is terrifying. 
I don't know, man. My buddy Xtian swears this place is awesome. And the food was OK. But not worth how expensive it was, to not be able to order what I want to order.

DON'T COME HERE
Waited an hour and a half to get one dish.... And they still didn't bring any other dish for another 30 mins.  The one dish they brought was so small, it only can feed four ppl.  Our group has 20 ppl!!  And the dish was cold!!!
This place is terrible.  Kept giving us bullshit excuses.... Bathroom is flooded and disgusting.  Mind as well piss all over the restaurant. 
Go to a better restaurant with better service and better food.  Waste of time.

Stopped by here for a family lunch after my husband and I married. This place is a massive dim sum restaurant, from the looks of the interior, i assume they host a lot of Chinese weddings here too.

Speaking of interior, I have to say it's largely outdated and tacky looking. The structural decorations on the ceiling and walls are quite beautiful though. Not that it seems to matter, this place gets busy! We probably had to wait 20 minutes to be seated, which was fine since we were waiting for some members.

We were seated at a large rounded table in the platformed section. Staffs were very accommodating and helpful in making space for my baby (this is not a place to bring babies and hardly any room for a capsule).

The food is very generic tasting and the selections mirrored much of what you'd get at every other dim sum restaurant. The pricing was good though and so was the tea we were served.

This place is very old school and seems to be a popular pick for large family gatherings. I'm one for variety and more modern food experiences, so I can't say I'd return on my own accord.

*p.s they provided valet parking during our visit, it might be a general service they provide in busy times.

Just had a Chinese new year dinner with family. Totally a rip-off
ordered the set dinner for $888.
1. supposedly you can select 1 soup out of 3, They told us only 1 is available, fine, after 2 dishes, then they told us that the soup was over cooked  and they will replace it with another one, which is a lower graded that listed on the $699 set dinner.
2. the fish was small, they covered the whole body with bean sprouts with tons of scallions and few pieces actual meat on top to cover up.
3. I bet those were canned Abalone.
4.  desert was served with Chinese cup cake came out of the fridge, didn't even bother to warm it up.

total came out with $1130 with tax and tips for 8 people. won't go there any more.

Poor business practice, lack of concern for their customers and sanitary issues in the kitchen, bathroom and serving areas.  This is a typical Chinese restaurant.  Food nothing to boast about.  I would only recommend this place if there was a zombie apocalypse and I knew you needed some nourishment before embarking on your survival journey.

Very very shitty service. I waited for half an hour for a table after getting a ticket for 2 and he ends up skipping my number and gave the table to someone who came a lot later then I did. The next thing that pissed me off was when I asked them when a particular dish was going to come out, he rudely tells me that he doesn't know, if it isn't out then it isn't out. Normally in these cases, they would tell you they will go ask, but he totally ignored me after that response and left. Wow....never have I ever seen such crappy service. No sorry at all. I guess this will be the last time I come here...I will take my business from people who actually try to work with the customer. Sucks when it's the lunar new year too...

This place is big and clean.  They have push cart dim sum so you can see what you're getting.  We didn't have to wait that long around 1:30pm for dim sum, maybe around 10-20 minutes.  They also offer valet parking, but I"m not sure how much you tip. 

The dim sum were fresh and delicious.   They have many dishes to choose including the regular har gow and siu mai.  It is a bit off the central Chinatown area so you need a car to get here.

We had our own table.  Whoo hoo!  Now, this is unheard of.  Usually, in Manhattan Chinatown, you have to share with others.  I felt the service was friendly and most waitresses spoke Cantonese, so I thought it was a pleasant experience.  Granted, it is a Wednesday at 9:30 am.  

First of all, we had a huge selection.  The prices are a bit steep, but the quality is definitely worth it.  We had some trouble flagging someone down to tabulate our bill, yet if you are not in a rush, then it is not a problem. Since we were watching the time (my friend had an appointment at 11:30 am) and we didn't want to bother the waitstaff, since it was busy, so we ended up there for another 10 minutes...so it's something to keep in mind to prepare wait time.  

Otherwise we had a grand time eating dim sum.  We were not rushed.  We had a lot of space and time to enjoy our meal.  We had hai gow, bean curd wrapped shrimp, white turnip cakes, shrimp dumplings with pork, lo mai gai (leaf wrapped chicken with stick rice), and cherng fun zha lern (deep fried rice roll--crueller?).  The dim sum here was not oily or small portion.  It is easy to share with a friend or if you bring your family.  It is also kid friendly.  I would definitely recommend it.

Lake Pavilion is a neat place to bring the family or a large group of friends. Prices are a little on the steep end, but it is well worth it when you consider the quality of food you get compared to some other restaurant dining experiences in Flushing.

Parking is convenient in the sense that there is Valet (only have to tip several $).

It can be a little tough to get the waiter's attention, but that is to be expected when you have so many tables and guests.

Overall a cool place in Flushing to check out and it's conveniently located next to the LIE if you're driving in by car.

The food is very tasty and the price is cheap,they have many option to choose from . $2 parking is available in the parking lot but please be advised sometime there is no parking available and inside is loud . staff is rude and over work.

Came here today for dim sum with my mom, my mom's friend, and her family. Holy moly the restaurant was super duper packed when we arrived at 12:30 pm. My mom's friend walked over to the podium to grab a number and the wait was about 10 minutes. When they finally called #11, we were directed to another room with a few tables already occupied. I love yum cha (飲茶) but sadly I can't consume tea because of health reasons so I ordered myself a can of Ginger Ale. 

My mom's friend and her family ordered for the table from the dim sum carts to other dishes such as Beef Chow Fun (it was bland though), Pork Chops Peking Style (::applause:: they did a great job...pork chops were fried before pouring the red sauce on them so the texture was perfect and not soggy), and Chicken & Salt Fish Fried Rice (my mom thought this dish had too much chicken pieces and not enough Salt Fish in it so thumbs down). 

Overall it was a good experience and next time I am bringing both of my parents here =)

If you want great dim sum in flushing this is the spot to go.  Parking is limited but that's because everyone likes this place and is packed on the weekend.   Great selection of dim sum and my go to Place for an authentic Cantonese style dinner.

They called me to say my order was ready and now ive been sitting for 10 minutes..they made me pay before..the food was pretty good though..not wonderful..but they have a pretty big menu..pretty expensive too..the generals tsos chicken came with no rice..id say 4 stars just because it's close by..but nothing so wrong to put it at 3

Went here this past Saturday at 11am for dimsum and the place was already packed! The dim sum here is pretty good. I had a seafood dumpling, beef noodle thing with sauce, vegetable chive dumpling and my favorite was the dessert a silky smooth tofu with sweet sauce, you must try this!

came here for dinner with my boyfriend's family and his mother's best friend. the food was decent and they gave us a hot towel to wipe our hands which is nice. Overall, the veggies were a bit oily but not bad. It is a fairly large restaurant and on a wednesday night, it was pretty quiet. It was so quiet that the wait staff kept asking us if we wanted to open the wine bottle we bought for his mother's friend. (Which we kept insisting NO we do not want to open it) but what wasn't so great was they took our cups to get us two cups of iced water that never came.
This is our go-to family dining restaurant. The food is good, service is fast and the prices are reasonable.

Very bad service , I never write bad review about any restaurants, but they pissed me off. the cooked food area gave me left over duck that are garbage . I called to complain but the manager told me it only cost me a few dollars so it is not a big deal. I am speechless . I came here often but I wl stop coming , there r other places much better than them. I wl give them zero rating if possible .           烧腊部见我没留意就给了我碎骨碎皮的鸭，像垃圾一样放在饭盒里，拿回家一看全部都要扔掉。买过这么多家烧腊这家可是让我开了眼界。经理的态度更是让人忍无可忍。第一次忍不住要动笔写下他们恶劣的服务态度。

Dined there Sunday and left my glasses on table. Called them 20 minutes after and they were too busy for me. I was a customer 20 minutes ago! Service goes a long way guys and the food is pretty mediocre canto food

Revising my rating. Been here about 20 times now for many diff family events. Food good. Dim sum is good but I def suggest knowing and speaking the language. Came here alone with my wife who knows alittle Cantonese but couldn't really get everythig we wanted and we got seated pretty far away.
Hustle and bustle on a Sunday, the food is decent and the cart girls speak English which is a plus if you have any questions good communication and decent dim sum what more can I ask for

This restaurant has definitely gotten much better for dim sum. There's a parking lot in the back for valet. They also get really busy during their typical dim sum hours so be prepared to wait for a table unless you come right when they open. The longest I usually have to wait is around half an hour since everything runs pretty quickly. Along with the dine in seating, there is a small shop where you can get a variety of Chinese barbeque items, bakery items, and take out dim sum.

They have the typical dim sum items such as chicken feet, shu mai, fried shrimp rolls, rice rolls and more. I particularly like the phoenix bun which is the salted egg yolk bun. It's something that needs to be eaten right when it gets to the table since that's when it is at its meltiest point. Although you might get overwhelmed with all of the ladies pushing the carts around trying to get you to buy everything off their cart, do not worry. They don't rush you to eat your food so you can still relax as you eat and socialize. The best part about dim sum is that you can see all the options that they have so even if you don't speak Chinese, you can just point to what you want. 

I recommend coming before 2 PM since they typically stop making some items around then and you'll end up only being able to choose from what is left over.

I came here for the first time for dinner for a family gathering. First thing first the parking lot is quite small and is valet parking only. If the lot is packed I can see problems finding parking on the street. The restaurant itself is pretty big and fairly nice. The food was hot and fresh we had an assortment of seafood items lobster, fish etc. also we had some beef and noodles and fried rice which was also very good. I would say this is a good place to have chinese cuisine. I have nothing to gripe about other than having a small parking lot. The food was definitely worth it. Highly recommend

I definitely would not recommend this restaurant. Their dishes are overpriced and the room is way too bright. There is zero privacy between the tables and would not return until these flaws are resolved.

Ah, the long history of Lake Pavilion. I remember back when it was the 90s, back when the Bank of China was "Lake Pavilion". When it was the simpler times. Y2K, LOL. Despite many years has passed, this restaurant has always stood on it's roots.   Quality and Integrity. PS: shout out to the lady that answers the phone. She's a saint. : D

UPDATE!
Since my last review, the place has gotten into a fire incident. It's been renovated and back in business.
I'm not sure if they are under new management? My family enjoy coming here now. Though, service varies from bad, okay and good. it really depends on who you get. The quality of food and service also depends on how busy they are. We try to avoid going on days that are too busy.

Just had dim sum brunch here, we got lucky to beat the crowd.  By the time we left, the place was packed and a bunch of people from the front entrance to the back were waiting to be seated.

This place is huge and the cart ladies pass by in regular intervals.  They offer the same food as any other dim sum place.  Service is slightly better because most servers speak English (my Chinese is kindergarten level haha) so it was easy to get what we want if it's not in the cart in front of us.

Oh, the only dim sum food that I didn't like was the minion bao.  It had black sesame filling but man it's bad (in my lifetime of eating - and I do love to eat - it takes a lot for my taste buds to find food that's unacceptable tastewise.).  So bad I couldn't finish it and left half on my plate (growing up, I was taught to never leave food on my plate no matter what.  But I'll make an exception with this minion bao).

ToTaLLy croWded... those letters sums up exactly how it felt, sooo many people on a weekend waiting, almost chaotic.   And yes, they will keep waiting if they have to - that also means their food is very solid!!!!  
Valet parking is also convenient, too.  Make sure to tip the guy.

Sharing tables is also an option - i actually do not mind.

Fantastic dim sum. This is my favorite cart-style dim sum place in Flushing, and I have eaten at them all. The Peking duck is okay, but there is better to be had a short drive away, and the carvers are not great for the most part. Poorly carved Peking duck is a travesty IMHO. Other dishes have been consistently good to very good, but not best in class.

My family and I went to this restaurant for a belated Mother's day celebration a few weeks ago.  Pretty good Cantonese food; prices are a little higher than usual; service was very friendly.  However, my big gripe is that they bring out Allllll the dishes we ordered all at once!  I just don't understand why they do this.  All the food ends up getting cold before you can enjoy them!  Asking them to pace the service doesn't help.  They blame it on the kitchen staff.   Next time, we  just won't order everything at once. They can't make everything at once if they don't know what you're going to order! Haha. (This will drive them bonkers but if you want hot food, this is the way to go).

Never go there again!! They have valet parking , but the guy parked my car at the up right Conner , which I believe where the kitchen is as I could see vent pipe thing there. And my whole car got grease on it, I went to the car wash, the regular car wash won't work, i have to do the detailing to my car and costing $200!!  And the food there is just ok.Not worthy to taking risk! Will never go again!!

We used to love this place. I'm surprised the place is always so packed even though the dim sum is so bad. The beef tripe was flavorless. The chicken feet was bland as well.  Most other items were either bad or barely edible. I guess they are so busy because they are the only dim sum place around there without having to drive to downtown Flushing.    We tried them again yesterday thinking it was maybe they had a bad day the last time. It's even worse now. I'm going to downtown Flushing to get real dim sum.

Came here for dim sum and I had a good experience on a weekday around noon. The wait was a few minutes and I shared a table with another couple which wasn't a problem. The carts come around frequently, and if you're not sure what something is you can always ask and they explain it. The prices are surprisingly cheap, even for their specials. The hostess and staff behind the counter where you pay were also very friendly. I'm not sure if I'd come here on a weekend based on other reviews, but weekdays are definitely a good time to come in.

I took my daughter over for a dim sum breakfast.  There was a nature show on the TV's all around the place about dung beetles eating, you guessed it, dung.  The Chinese woman across the round table from me put down her chopsticks in disgust and left.  The dim sum was good, but we had to fight for it, we were ignored.  
My husband I returned a while later and walked into the restaurant when it was almost empty for an early dinner/late lunch.  Two men were standing at the front arranging things.  They ignored us.  We waited.  They continued to be "busy" and didn't register our presence.  A Chinese couple walked in, they were immediately greeted, in English, and were seated as we were ignored.  We walked out.  We live blocks away, but will never return,

How did this place get so bad? This used to be my go to spot. Since the fire the service and the food has gone way downhill. And they charged us some arbitrary bai ren prices. They push cold crappy dishes and when I ask how much? They don't know.  I literally heard the woman say charge them 8$ for Xiao long bao. And because I speak Chinese I recoiled at the price. Then she says 7 something in English. Like I'm supposed to not care about the prices? Shady. 7.99$ probably. Ugh. Like they don't know the best XLB is right across the street at Kung Fu? Their dough is thick and chewy, the shu mai was COLD. At 11:30 no one is in the kitchen making anything what are they doing in there. It must have changed hands. I'm soooo disappointed. Totally sucked. Honestly, I think they're charging a premium because of parking. Won't be back for a long time.

Haven't been here since the fire but the food has definitely gotten worse. The presentation was nice but the taste was mediocre. We kept flagging down a waiter to get simple service needs. We also had non stop visiting flies. Very disappointing to say the least.

The restaurant is a bit out of the way since you need to either walk 20 min or take a bus from main street Flushing.  The food is quite good.  We came here several time for their king crab specials.  The restaurant offers to cook for you two or three ways.  The price for the crab was slightly cheaper compared to the restaurants closer to main street.  Service is better than the average service you can get from a typical Chinese restaurant.  Interior is also your typical Chinese banquet style decor, nothing spectacular.  If you go to any non-Chinese restaurant for king crab, first, you are not going to get a live one that the restaurant will fish it out of the tank and show it to you, second, you are not going to get the same price per lb.  Overall, for the price and quality of the food, you get your month worth.

This review is for dim sum and lunch. Solid dim sum with a large variety of selections compared to other busy dim sum places in the area. Always a wait during prime time on weekends. Recommend getting there before 11:00 or after 1:30 on weekends for less of a wait time. We also ordered a shredded pork chow mein which was delicious. Service is adequate but not the primary attraction here. Speak up if you need something!

I am very upset about their disrespectful and arrogant manners. There were so many people here because it's a holiday today. I came with my family. We finished and my dad and I went to the front desk to pay. 
Our bill was $90.40 we gave this lady with glasses our card and I was filling out my tips. I put down $9.00 as tips. That was 10%. Including tax we paid $107.40 in total. And this lady took a look and asked me why I give such little tips. So I told her I think I gave enough. 
I was talking in Cantonese to my family so she thought I was FOB and said to me, "were u from New York? Here everyone knows that you have to tip at least 15% if the service it's good you should tip up to 20%." 
I then told her "miss, i paid my bill. And I put down some tips. First of all it's not required for me to pay any tips at all."
She then went on and said, " I'm not trying to argue with you. But little girl I'm teaching you. I'm trying to help you here. To learn the rule in New York. I don't know if you grew up here but even my son knows that you should pay at least 15% of tips. It's for ur benefits to know."
I was so triggered that I laughed. And my dad next to me was like what are you guys arguing about. And he told me not to make a scene just tip them more and was asking the lady back for the bill and asked "how much more do we owe I'll just pay." I felt so wronged. I grabbed him and told him we didn't do anything wrong and he shouldn't pay any more than we think they deserve. 
I had my arm leaning on the counter and the lady grabbed my arm and keep saying she's not trying to have an argument. And she turned to my dad and said, "is this your daughter? You should teach her better. You should go home and teach her about the rules." 
At that moment my mind went blank because I could not believe some one would be so mean and disrespectful to have the audacity to say such thing. My dad didn't want to cause a scene even tho he hated that she said that about me. 
I don't think I'll ever want to come back to this place again.

Normally I don't write a review unless it is super good and very unique or Terrible and people should stay away. Average restaurant I normally not write anything. But today was something I must write. 

This is a dimsum place I always go to (always) why? Because it's away from Central Flushing, next to the highway (LIE). Street parking not as bad if u are willing to walk 2 resident blocks. 

I come here with my family normally with s big party 6-12 people, of course a wait time for such large party. Foods are good service good ok, cleanse (ehh) just ask waiter to replace it if dirty. Never had an issue. (AVERAGE)

Today I came here as a party of 3 they inner section (attach is a picture I took from another Yelper of this place) just want to give you a sense of where. 

The cart can't reach where we were sitting. And they will skip you. The only people that would come is the hand held ones. Yes the dimsum cart will ignore you. I was able to flag a waiter to tap the dimsum cart lady, ask her what she have and she goes and tell me I can't get there and you will need to come out and see. Like WTF, you can just tell me what you have and that's it. The next person this lady tell the whole lost to the customer which was sitting outside of the edge where the cart pass.

Next 3 cart pass, Had to get up run to the cart and pick up my own dimsum which each plate is very HOT. 

To the owner if he/she is reading this. Table layout very important. Something like this would affect how a customer is treated by your employees. Larger party gets treated much better.

*tip: share table will normally be in the route where the cart lady travel. Will have a easier time to get food than the table I got. (Unless you don't want to share table with stranger then good luck)

Food: 4 star ( Dimsum only )
Waiting Time: 5-10 mins and some time 20-30mins depending how busy.
Waiter: 4 stars
Dimsum cart lady: 3star (for today 1 star)
Cleanse: 3 star
 
It not like I'm giving a 1 star. still gets a 3 star for being average. Just want to vent my frustration on going to a restaurant and not get food service and had to chase down carts get my own foo and bring back to my table (hot plates)

ima just do take out for now, never an issue with take out. Save the hassle.

I've been coming here for dimsum for years. Used to enjoy this place as much as other dimsum places but today we were seated on one of those tables in the middle row. THIS IS NOT THE PROBLEM! All other servants are doing their job just fine! And we had no problem ordering at all.  Until this one lady who was just pushing the cart with food, passed by, as she was talking to someone else, not paying attention to us who were waving our hands at her. Then, finally she saw us, asked us "what do you want?", we asked her what she has, she told us to get up and look ourselves. Didn't even bother to tell us what she has, or at least just tell us she has "buns".  I appreciate everyone else, I even got up to pick up what I ordered when I saw the other servants were having trouble getting to us, I understand the job is not easy. But this lady--her attitude, not paying attention, didn't care about the customers, is a NO.

We went to New Lake Pavilion for dim sum. The dim sum is pushed around on little carts so you can see what you like & order it. This review is for dim sum only.

DIM SUM summary (I use ^ to indicate a half-star and * for a full star. So, ***^ means 3.5 stars):

****^ BBQ pork buns are very good. The filling is good, but the pastry is great, flaky but also a little soft and gummy, excellent texture

***^ Steamed sticky rice chicken wrapped in lotus leaf is pretty good. The filling is tasty & the flavours get absorbed into the sticky rice. The texture of the rice is good.

*** Fried Taro root dumpling is flaky and puffy on the outside, and soft on the inside. This was okay but not as flavourful or crispy as I'd like

*** Salt Water Dumpling is solid. Nothing exceptional, but tasted okay

**^ Braised chicken feet taste okay. Unfortunately, the chicken feet weren't cooked as much as they should be so that the flavours would get absorbed in better. There were only 3 feet in the dish, cut into halves. The dish is mostly peanuts (on the bottom). 

**^ White Radish cake is so-so, with not enough radish or wok flavour. This is usually one of my favourites, but this version was not very tasty.

**^ Rice noodle rolls with scallions are very soft, and lacking flavour. Most of the flavour comes from the soy & hoisin sauces that are added on top, but there was not enough sauce. It would have been better with sesame sauce.

** Shrimp dumplings with chives is disappointing & not flavourful. There was hardly any shrimp. Usually, I'd want these to be full of plump, succulent shrimp 

*^ Stuffed pepper is bland. I wouldn't recommend.

* Chestnut cake is sweet. The texture is okay, but I'm not a fan of how it tastes. I wouldn't want this again.

SERVICE is good.
