PARKING is difficult to find in the area. But they do have Valet Parking right next to the restaurant, which is well-serviced.

Dim sum: 3 stars at best
Service: 0 star if I could

Dim sum was mediocre at best. What really grinds my gear is how extremely rude the staff was. I'm talking about you, male host who screamed at me and my 85yo grandma (!!!!) before we even got a chance to sit down.

I was helping my grandma walking out of the bathroom and this host lunged at us and asked us what number we have. I told him our number. He started yelling at us about how they've called our number a couple times already. My grandma was super sweet and apologized a couple times... BUT WE WERE IN THE BATHROOM. That's not how you treat your customers, especially not the elderly.

120% will not return.

We went to this restaurant at 9 a.m. for dinner. This morning tea actually had two dishes searched. I didn't expect that such a famous place had sour and rotten dishes. The service attitude was very bad. I had a very bad dining experience.

New Lake Pavilion is one of my auntie's favorite dim sum place in Flushing. The decor here is super exaggerated and it is also a perfect place for Chinese holding their wedding ceremony. They served dim sum every day before 3pm and Cantonese cuisines all day. 

They had a wide variety of dim sum served by cart and most of their dim sum were delicious and authentic. Our favorites were steamed spare ribs and salted egg custard buns. The ribs were well cooked, chewy and tasty flavored with braised taro. The salted egg custard buns were a must try and super addictive. 

Their service was also authentic - super rude and reluctant but kind. They have their parking lot but it was always crowded and impossible to find a place.

New Lake Pavilion is located right off the LIE and has valet parking as well as limited metered parking available. This has been one of my favorite places to get dim sum but I feel lately the quality of the food as well as the service has been on the decline. Their har gow used to be packed with ridiculously succulent, juicy shrimp and bits of bamboo but on my last two visits, the filling was mushy and overcooked. Their wrapper also broke apart as soon as I picked it up with chopsticks, a further sign of shoddy craftsmanship. 

New Lake Pavilion also used to come up with really inventive and unique small bites but I haven't felt particularly wowed by any of their offerings this past year. That is not to say everything has gone downhill-- there are still some dim sums I enjoy here. Their custard buns are very pretty and the intensely milky flavor form both the bun and generous custard filling is delicious. Their cheong fun are generally good, with a good slippery and soft, slightly chewy texture. I like to order one of their specialty cheong fun which comes wrapped around crispy fried shrimp paste. Unfortunately, these two dishes alone are not an incentive enough to make the trek over from Brooklyn.

I came here for dim sum over the weekend and I have to say, they were fantastic. With a group of three we were able to order quite a few dishes and all the dishes we had were very well executed.

The size of their dim-sum was generous and they all came out piping hot and fresh. I particularly enjoyed their fried eggplant because it was fully stuffed with shrimp paste (instead of pork fat), which made the eggplant taste silky smooth.

Their special shrimp rolls were also tasty as well. Aside from the shrimp I think they also added the fried dough which gave an amazing texture to the rolls and their shrimp was jumbo enough to feel like a mouthful.

As for service, the cart ladies were overall good! They were eager to show us all the dishes they had in their cart and if a particular dish wasn't there, they would go and get it. For me, that added step was pleasant especially when I didn't even ask them to.

When we arrived, their was a bit of a wait time. We arrived 12:15pm and it took about 35 minutes before we got seated. Regardless, it was worth the wait, the guy calling out the number was on top of his game, and I didn't mind waiting so much because watching the guests dine was enjoyable enough.

We had a birthday banquet there. The food is so so, but the service is VERY BAD. The servants are in a rush, and I left the table for something else for about 5 minutes, and they came to try to take my plate several times. 很糟糕的服务，食物质量也一般，不推荐！
Dim sum is good but I wasn't happy with the extra $2 charge for HOT WATER for refilling my teapot? Seriously? Also mandatory valet tips is $2.

This was a nice dimsum place with private rooms that you can reserve. Super crowded though but what do you expect - probably similar at most other dimsum places on a weekend. They have a good variety of dimsum options and if you have never been, I definitely recommend to try at least once! Just a side note, their bathrooms are near the doors to outside so in the wintertime, make sure to wear your jacket on your way to the bathroom so you don't get cold!

First visit = Last visit.
I've lived in flushing for over 30 years and always wondered why my family and relatives have NEVER ever been to this place.  Today, we had limited time and decided to try Lake Pavilion for dim sum only because it's right off the LIE.  The food is average, the dim sum selection is pretty decent with all the staples.  The waiters were polite and the cart ladies provided usual chinese restaurant quality service: no nonsense, no chit chat, no niceties, just quick servive.
For average food, the prices are a bit high. Theres also way too much msg.  When I have to keep downing water I know something's wrong with the food.
As someone else also pointed out, its $2 for tea (hot water) refill and the valet will demand $2 tip even if you park and drive out your car yourself!

This is my second or third visit this year.  Each meal has offered many tasty dishes but definitely not consistent. Service is hit or miss as well based on the house being full or not. I was here on a Sunday night at 7pm on this most recent visit and had a private room booked for 12. Purposely wanted the Karaoke feature but it was not working well. Either low battery in the microphones or they were broken. Either way, the restaurant made no effort to fix/replace. That was not cool. Still managed to watch music videos and play music at least.  It was a birthday banquet so not cool that the birthday boy didn't get to sing.

Onto the food, the classic dishes seemed to be quite tasty. However,  to the trained eye, each dish was not to the normal serving standard for Cantonese fare. Don't get me wrong, everything tastes fine as ordered but execution was the downfall.  Some plates were plated well and served as expected but the timing was off. Everything came out almost at once instead of a spaced out pace so dish upon dish was getting cold. We just couldn't eat at the pace.  The order they were presented was just as confusing.

The fish maw soup we ordered (no photo!) was served for 10 and I didn't get to photograph it since they divided it up per bowl instead of showing us the full soup bowl /serving size. That's not normal in itself. And with soup especially, there totally should have been left over for refills or seconds. So that I found off-putting.

The good:
Salmon sashimi platter, served over ice and accompanied by a hand carved taro statue for decor. Fun. Pricey but fresh so we enjoyed it.

Skip the sliced rib steak, not much flavor and it was very fatty.  Order the lamb chops or the T-bone steak instead.  Both are better cuts of meat.

The longevity noodles were ok and so were the beef chow fun but not enough for me to write any more. It was just inconsistent from the last time I was here.

Overall still a decent place to eat but it would not be my first choice in Flushing.





The parking lot is insane, valet only and yet there's still no room! Forget coming here on a Saturday night, by 6:30pm, all the spots are gone! Also, street parking is not easy but it is a residential zone so worth trying your luck. Just stay off Northern Blvd.

The waiters here has the nerve to ask for more tip.  Haha.  No face money beggars.....

Dimsum isnt that bad but overpriced and bad attitudes from waiters with no shame.

Dinner at this seafood restaurant was very nice.  They provided us with a private dining room even though it was not a request.  We had the special king crab, which was costly, but well worth it.  We chose the smallest available which was at about 6-7 pounds which they brought to our table. 
 It was prepared three ways, steamed with aromatics (ginger, scallions, black bean sauce), stir fried with eggs and then the top shell was fried and stuffed with sticky rice.  Definitely the best way was steamed with aromatics as the sweetness of the crab was just so succulent in every bite.  The stir fried one was good too.  The top shell stuffed with sticky rice was a bit of a disappointment.  We thought the fried rice would have been imbued with the essence of the crab, but it was not.  Additionally, we requested that the rice not have peanuts which the manager told us he would put in the request but could not provide any assurance, but, just like all other Chinese restaurants, it came with peanuts.

We had some other dishes, which were hit and miss, lamb chops - a hit, a steamed/fried whole fish - miss, stuffed tofu with conch - ok, etc...

Overall it was a good experience.  They get a star for the private room, lose a star for the peanuts and get a star for the king crab.  

There is valet parking in the back for those who are interested.

One of my family's favorite dim sum places 

Pros:
- If you have a large enough group you can request a room - somewhat quieter so you're able to hear your relatives speak 
- Plenty of dim sum even after 2pm 
- Waiters/waitresses are super efficient 
- Nice, rowdy, and homey atmosphere 

Cons:
- Parking can be a nightmare even though they have valet parking in the back. May the odds be in your favor.
The service here is unbelievably bad, they are not interested in hearing your concerns but rather to keep this moving. Would not come again

Usually extremely busy during dim sum hours. The parking lot gets full easily and the surrounding neighborhood street parking is quite difficult. Variety of dim sum keeps my parents happy. The carts are plentiful and continue to come around constantly. They offer private rooms for parties as well. Food is generally good and location is right off of the LIE so I don't have to drive into flushing where parking is even more limited and traffic can make it a nightmare.

Very busy restaurant on a Sunday late morning, but the wait was only around half an hour.  Aside from the main dining room, there are lots of smaller rooms that had a few tables. The food was fresh and there was a lot of variety. I love that they still serve dim sum via carts! Keeps the food nice and hot. Loud and rowdy just like a dim sum restaurant should be. Parking is a bit of a disaster as their parking lot fills up quickly and there doesn't seem to be a lot of street parking in the area. They also have a take out area for Chinese bbq, steamed rice noodles, buns and drinks.
I recommend them for dim sum and dinner parties.  The food is great and service is exceptional.  Parking is available in the back!

We had a large family dinner here on Christmas night. The restaurant is massively understaffed. It takes 20 minutes to get anyone's attention or to get anything, like even a glass of water. All the dishes we ordered ranged from meh to okay. The oysters were huge but tasted strange. The walnut shrimp, which is a standard dish that any restaurant should be able to nail, was unappealingly yellow and not crispy. They also did not give us any complimentary fruit or dessert as is standard for these types of restaurants.

I couldn't remember why we ever returned after the first time so we came back since the location is ideal. I will not go back unless I was desperate. The service staff is horrible - they kept walking by us and ignoring our request for assistance. They argued with us about the tea we wanted - they brought over a random tea (that we would never order) and when we asked for a different one, gave us attitude saying that we had already requested one. The food was mediocre at best and pretty much just passable. The bill came out to over $100 and we typically average at $80 for dim sum at other restaurants. To top it off, when we left to retrieve our car, a pick up van partially blocked us in. Luckily my husband is pretty good at maneuvering the car so we were able to squeeze our way out or else I would've been even more upset with dim sum.

Came for the dim sum service on CNY. Seated right away as we were a small group of 3. We were in the middle and largely ignored by the cart ladies. Had to spent half of my time there hunting for the dishes we wanted. We didn't stay very long as to be conscientious of the holiday and business. Food was okay. Nothing to write about, nothing to complain about either. Good variety, stuck to the familiar cart service instead of menu ordering. Very well staffed for the day. Black jackets will help find dishes you want for you, otherwise if you have been unlucky enough to be stick in the inner tables, be prepared to walk up and peer into carts to order.

I come here all the time for dimsum.  It is always crowded on weekends.  Unless you come when it opens, be prepared to wait.  The wait is worth it as more selection comes out towards the afternoon.  They also have a side take out store that only takes cash though.  You can also get really good pork or fish sandwhiches for 1.75.

Was there on 3/6/20 and the food was fantastic. was there for dim sum. 
people need to come out and support this business. the staff is awesome, very accommodating!! the food is tasty, not salty or msg laden. 
people are scared now, but i went, and am glad i did.

Dim sum is one of my favorite meals. And I've eaten a lot of it over the years. I've recently stumbled on to New Lake and it's a new favorite! So many items, hot and delicious! It's a bit away from the bustling part of Flushing, but that doesn't mean this place doesn't get busy*. There are so many different, delightful dishes I've not seen at other dim sum places. But you'll also find the dishes you're familiar with. The women who push the copious carts are kind and love to explain what they have when they see I'm uncertain. 

*i went again today and it was disturbingly empty. I've read about the dip in Chinese businesses, but this was shocking. If you don't come here (and you should!), get out there and show some love to struggling businesses.

I always like to give a place another chance and they continue to disappoint. Service and food was subpar. The lobsters was so small and tasteless and they charge $26 for each lobster. The restaurant was not busy but I had to asked three times for a bowl of rice. The pan fried flounder was maybe ten chunks of fish on top of this huge flounder. Disappointed again.
This place is finally open after being closed during the pandemic.  The takeout section is open with outdoor seating provided.  Food is as delicious as I remember it to be.  Yay!!!

This place serve dim sum at this time. Great outdoor seating and  good amount of distance between tables.  This place have tent set up for customers to be seated and eat. The roofs are sort of  heat resistance  with silver lining to try to diminish the heat coming from the sun. 

The   2  bad things, I can say is taro cake is cook for too long and dry up.  Also the salty egg buns  are not runny as  it suppose to but still taste good. 

The food is a average but cannot be too choosy at this time of you are cravings for  dim sum.

4/10
Disclaimer this is the covid rating and not the normal rating. So let's start off with that I have been here a couple times in the past and if it wasn't covid I would give it a 5.5/10 from my past experiences(it's in the pricier side). 

So this is outdoor dining with a lot of shade so that was good as it wasn't that hot eating outside. However, there aren't any dim sum aunties pushing the metal carts around and you order thru a paper. Now here's some issues with it. The paper is in Chinese only and I can't read Chinese but I can speak it so I had to request the servers to check things off for me. That isn't too bad but if you don't speak or read Chinese ordering will be a hassle.

Food problems are that the food aren't hot. Anything that's not on a bamboo tray was cold. Aka any rice rolls, chive dumplings, etc. I believe they can't really put those things into the metal cart steamers like precovid days The bamboo tray ones are fine in temp.

Shrimp rice roll 2/10
 Cold and slightly hard cause it stuck together. Tasted okay but the texture and temperature really ruined it. 

Chives shrimp dumplings 3/10
 Tasted good and also cold but these dumpling are usually only like warm anyway. So the temp difference wasn't too much and didn't ruin it a lot. However, not pan fried enough so the skin texture was also not great to start with. 

Shumai 4/10
A lot of dim sum place confuse what shumai is. Loading it up on shrimp and not enough pork. Tasted okay but not truly a shumai just a glorified shrimp dumpling.

Beef balls 5/10 
The best thing we ate here. Tasted good and large portions.  The consistency was a little too soft tho. The meat consistency was too soft and felt like they may of used a little to much baking soda to soften the meat before the grinded it. Slightly tighter and bouncier consistency would add so much to each bite and would of made it a lot better.

Steam Spare ribs 5/10
 Tasted good but wasn't as flavorful as i wanted. Maybe a little more black beans and cooking wine would of helped.

1/10 congee with slim pork and thousand year old egg 
 Went with a friend who doesn't dim sum much. Yea just  dim sum diners never served good congee in general. If you want congee go to a congee restaurant . Salt wasn't mixed well too watery clearly used starch as a thickener vs slow cooking the rice for hours etc. aka just don't get it

Egg tart 2/10
  There's no egg tarts in America that can compete with authentic ones made across the ocean but egg tarts were not fresh or warm. Same with the congee dim sum  really isn't the place to be getting egg tarts 

All in all the food was sub par good experience as it's been nearly half an year since I had dim sum. If your looking for quality dim sum today this isn't the place. But if your looking for a lite version of it so you can reminisce of the simpler days of getting dim sum this place is passable.
Got takeout yesterday for the entire family. They're new menu is limited but had some essentials for us like chicken feet and short ribs. Would go back again.

Ordered some dim sum for take out yesterday. When I got back home and found out 3 missing... there's no way for me to check at the counter bcoz it's all packed. Don't think they will refund me the money. And the food is just ok.

Ordered dim sum to go last month. It was quick and easy. We called in and the gentleman was really nice and helpful. We are dim sum regulars so we knew what we wanted already but did ask for some suggestions for things we might have missed in our order. The food was well packaged when we picked it up. The food was good.  It wasn't great but it was good for take out when you need it at 11am during a pandemic.

Went Saturday around noon for outdoor dining. It was understandably crowded and there was a wait but once we sat down for dim sum the food came quickly. We were new to the process but the waiter was polite and helped us navigate ordering. We left stuffed. The pork buns were the best and you can't beat the price!
Please do double checking your order on the spot carefully before leaving the restaurant!!!

It's alright.  Nothing to write home about.

It gets very crowded.  The parking lot gets packed.  The line to  the little parking lot blocks up the whole side street and corner, making a nuisance for the area.  But, I think that's mostly due to its location away from downtown Flushing.  It's the only big dim sum place in the area.  

The service is typical of these types of Chinese restaurants that cater mainly to Chinese.  It's brusk.  

And it's quite dirty.  Esp the take out side.  

We only come here bc we don't want  to drive into the heart of Flushing.  I really wish these kinds of places would clean up a bit, train their staff to be more courteous, and to stop wiping their bare hands all over their faces while serving food.  But, the crowds tell them they have enough business to not give a damn. 

Update Sept 8, 2020:
When you go order roast port etc from the take out counter, make sure to order LESS than what you really want.  They will ALWAYS give you a half a pound more of whatever you order.  Part of is our own fault for not complaining about it.  Also, we've usually waited on line to buy the stuff so we just take the extra large order and go on our way.  Sneaky!!
I would give them a 5 if the staff were friendlier. The food is delicious.  We order several dishes and we weren't disappointed.  The overall comfort level was not welcoming.

Excellent, traditional dim sum and easy to get to location. The service is efficient, the dim sum menus are in chinese but I was able to dictate my usual 8-10 dim sum cravings and she got them down for me. Their egg tarts are a stand out - super flaky dough. All in all a great place, everything tasted fresh. During Covid, they have plenty of outdoor seating and you are given disposable ware which is nice, there are no carts going around, you place your order and the order is brought out all at once. Prices are reasonable as well.

This rating is based on their operation during Covid-19. We have a party of 12 for outdoor seating dinner. The taste is definitely not the same as before. None of the dishes was hot, it was just warm. One of dish (beef with black bean source) was not fully cooked. We have to ask the waiter to bring it back to the kitchen and cook a little bit longer. Service was below average. Each person will use paper plates and cups with throwaway chopsticks. They never bother to change the paper plates for you. Price was up a little bit which is understandable.

It's been a year since my family has gotten together. A reservation was made for 5pm at this restaurant which we last visited back in December during normalcy. Upon arrival gone are the days with valet parking as one parks their own vehicle at any available space. At this time, this place only offers outdoor dining and takeout. We were greeted by one of the staff wearing masks and lead us inside a big white tent to our table for dinner. We ordered pan fried sole, crispy chicken with lemon sauce, sweet & sour pork, beef with broccoli, pan fried noodles with assorted seafood, beef fried rice and fried calamari. Wooden disposable chopsticks were offered but we decided on plastic utensils. The food came in huge portions that were deliciously tasty with no complaints and had to take doggy bags home. We've been coming here for years and highly recommend this place.

Got takeout yesterday and we received no soy sauce for the multiple plates of Ha Cheung and rice noodle rolls that we ordered. Additionally, the plates/containers that they gave us were low quality and easily cracked open, causing some sort of leakage. After we complained to them, they decided to not apologize, but instead, shifted the blame to us saying that we did not check the entirety of the bag of takeout food to find it. The workers there also did not want to admit that they messed up the order when the manager asked them, which is not to be surprised. What better way is there to shift the blame than to blame the customers? We offered to provide them with evidence showing what was in the entirety of the bag we got for take out but for them, ignorance is a bliss.

Yummy nice Chinese dim sum place. We tried this place during pandemic. We do take out because there's a parking lot outside. We can just grab and leave. They offer many choices of dim sum with good quality. Everything taste yummy. Shu Mai and egg yolk bun are my favorites. Haven't tried dine in yet, will do as soon as the pandemic is over .

I've had the more traditional dimsum dishes here. Definitely the best in queens. I've been here before covid and the wait on the weekend are at least an hour. Recently I've only done take out and it's been pretty  smooth.  I call in (yes, they speak fluent english) ahead of time and go straight to the pick up line.

My go-to Cantonese cuisine restaurant for years and loved coming here for Chinese Banquets pre-Covid. Currently, only paper plates, cups and wooden chopsticks. For a traditional family style dinner, I would recommend:
1) Crab meat and fish maw soup
2) Fried half/whole chicken (super thin crispy skin)
3) Fried Shrimp with Mayo/walnut
4) Abalone and Sea Cucumber (if you're adventurous to try a speciality)
5) Filet sole fish (served with snap peas)
6) Fried tofu stuffed with shrimp
7) E-fu/longevity noodles with crab meat 
8) Double lobster with scallions

Service is awful! Been there for dim sum and shrimp rice roll and shrimp fried roll were cold. They didn't do anything or say anything when I complained. Had dinner there and all waiters give me feeling like I owe their money. They should have better management  and better service especially during this hard time. Not feeling welcomed.

Lake pavilion has always been my go to place for dim sum when in Flushing! I recently went on a Sunday Morning for take out & it was definitely packed for both takeout & dine in. I tried calling ahead to order but the line was dead (I'm assuming because it's usually really busy on weekends). We waited about 25-30 mins for our takeout order which is definitely quite a bit but again, Sunday mornings is when everyone goes to get dimsum. If you don't want to wait, I would recommend going on a weekday! (Hopefully their phone line works then).

I ordered some dim sum along with beef chow fun. The beef chow fun was delicious!!!! Due to covid, you have to check what kind of dishes you want and they bring it out to you. The beef tripe was cold when it was bought out, so disappointed as I love beef tripe during dim sum. They have out paper plates and cups for sanitary. The cups for tea was so tiny :( definitely not the same dimsum vibes as pre covid.

Ordered dim sum for take out this Saturday, the price is reasonable and the food is delicious. One less star is because most dishes were almost cold, need to reheat after I got home. Ordered 7 dishes and one was wrong. They gave me beef tender instead of pepper beef ribs.

Food:
Their dim sum quality has gone slightly down during Covid, but even so their shrimp dishes are all still so good. Highly recommend the shrimp gao and the golden shrimp roll.

Service:
The servers are very attentative and the orders came out FAST.

Ordering process:
They have limited outdoor seating and they don't roll around the carts during this time. You are given a paper chinese menu sheet and you mark X next to the dish along with the quantity you'd like.

This place has mediocre dim sum.  I came here on a Sunday morning and it was really crowded, but we still got seats after a long wait. The food was okay and nothing amazing. I generally really enjoy dim sum but this place was ok. If you're in flushing, there are plenty of other places with better dim sum.

I've been going to this restaurant for dim sum for a few years now and it's good. A bit pricey but it beats fighting the traffic going into flushing so I'll pay a little extra. However take out dinner is a whole different ball of wax. On two separate occasions, I asked that they not put garlic or onions in the dishes and both times they did! Furthermore, the noodles looked like a mash up of two different dishes - gross! My noodle dish didn't call for curry but a section of it was curried. That's just disgusting! I gave it one star for the dim sum but I'll never patron here again!

We ordered a platter for 5pm. They called and asked us to come early at 4:30pm for pick up. It was not ready at 4:30 or 5pm. I waited almost an hour and then they gave us someone else's platter that had been sitting on the table. The food was cold. It was so disorganized, with no social distancing! Very annoying, wasted my time. I told my family to never order from them again.

Look what COVID has done to a once proud dim sum house... I recall coming here a few years ago with my family, it was bustling with dim sum carts and ladys yelling out like a street market.  The food was fresh and steaming and brought right to your table.  The joy of looking over the items in each cart, picking out your favorites and perhaps trying a new thing or two.
Those days are gone.
The crowds are now replaced with socially distant tables set up at least 6 feet apart.  The dim sum carts are now replaced with a picture menu where you order what you want and they bring it out to you.

Ambience - the crowds, noise, and carts are part of the experience.  Without those, it's like going to the circus and not seeing any animals.  The use of plastic utensils and paper plates doesn't improve the experience either.

Food - I guess it's the same food, but the ambience affects my taste buds.  It just doesn't taste as fresh...

Service - staff size is reduced due to COVID.

TL/DR - if you have a craving for dim sum, this is what passes for dim sum during COVID.  This is essentially Dim Sum to go, but they let you eat there.
Their quality is getting worse and worse.  The meats in the Dim Sum is RAW.  WTF? I hope I don't get food poisoning.  This will be the last time I go there.
New Lake is a solid dim sum restaurant conveniently located right off the LIE on Main St and away from the madness of Flushing. They get busy but still are quick and efficient. Come get sum dim sum.

Easily one of the best dim sum in Flushing. My favorite is their beef rice rolls. It's gotta be minced meat and not sliced beef. They also have a bakery in the front that sells roast meats. Their menu is really big and everything I tried is delicious. Been coming here for years now.

One star is way to good for this place! MUST AVOID THIS ESTABLISHMENT AT ALL COST!!! Extremely poor services. All waiters/ waitresses are rude, nasty especially the floor supervisor they treated us like we asking for free foods. PLEASE YOUR BUSINESSES TO WHERE ELSE!!!!! AGAIN, AVOIDING THIS PLACE!!!

This is my family's go to place for dim sum or dinner whenever we're in Flushing. They're located right next to the highway and have valet parking. The food is always fresh, delicious, and cooked without being drenched in excessive oil. The interior is also a lot nicer than other restaurants in Flushing and they definitely have enough room to spread everyone out six feet in order to abide by COVID-19 regulations.

My favorite dish is Walnut Shrimp. The jumbo shrimp is always lightly breaded like a tempura. The shrimp isn't swimming in mayonnaise, and the candied walnuts are always crisp and subtly sweet. I like that the dish also comes with steamed broccoli so we can have some veggies with our meal.

The lamb chops are a big hit for those looking for some turf with a lot of flavor. They are a good portion size and  the meat is always nice and tender.

According to my parents, the razor clams are cleaned really well before being cooked so there's not a lot of sand residue or taste in the dish. The sauce for the razor clams is like a garlic sauce but there is a slight kick to it. After all, it is a seafood dish so some spice is expected.

The sautéed sliced conch with squid and fried tofu is also one of my family's favorites. There's something for everyone in that dish. Fried tofu for those not big on meat. Sautéed vegetables for those who want a light vegetable dish without all the heavy sauces. Sliced conch and squid for those who want to have a bit of surf for their meal but don't wanna go all out.

Their menu is pretty extensive so whether you want to go full Asian or Asian American, they have something for everyone. Also, I'm all for the Asian dining experience but this place isn't as crowded or as noisy as your typical Chinese restaurant so you can have a real conversation at the table without having to scream over other people.

I go to them for morning dimsum when I crave some. I love for the fact that it's super authentic, just that the workers there don't understand much English and it's a hassle to order. I've used it as an opportunity to learn Chinese - for food- but it can be tough for someone who is not familiar with the culture. They take cash only at the take out counter, but if you bring the bill inside, you can pay with credit card too.

Not ready for full capacity.  Every table was full but the restaurant did not have sufficient staff to service all of the tables.  3 of the 8 orders of dim sum did not show up.  Waiter took my teapot to refill but never brought it back.  I ordered a plate of noodles but a half hour later the kitchen said it never got the order.  I really wanted to support this restaurant post-COVID but management needs to do better.  Instead of waiting forever for the food, I left hungry.

Good food, fast service, easy parking. Went there around 3:30pm and they were not serving dim sum (will come try next time!) So we ordered from regular menu. I love their seafood dishes, like steamed fish, walnut shrimp and seafood soup. Very fresh and delicious.
My family comes here often for dim sum and they also have valet parking. A lot of their dim sum dishes are tasty and they have a pretty good selection!

7.6/10

Dim sum: good experience; most of the food was very good; most meat was too fatty, but pretty flavorful; chicken was not very good, pretty dry; everything with shrimp was great though

If you're in the area or not in the area, definitely give it a try m. Dim sum is not for everyone, but this place is exceptional in its food and service. 5 out of 5 stars, and now my go-to dim sum restaurant

Great food, large portions and chef did a good job in accommodating  our requests for less salt and oil. 

Our dinner meal consisted of:
Steamed Sole or flounder which was amazing and healthy. The simple scallion and sauce over rice was so amazing appetizing. 

Braised E-fu noodle with seafood was full of squid, large shrimp, scallops- super delish and what a deal for $19!

Snow pea sprout and crab meat- one of my favorite veges topped with chunks of crab gravy.

Our first time back to indoor dimsum since the pandemic began. Everything used was disposable. You circle your items on the paper menu and they'll bring the food out to you.  Too bad the menu was all in Chinese. Luckily mom was there to read it. Food was very good. Tables were socially distanced but it was still very loud inside. Glad to see some things are still normal.

Nice place and  it is always packed  on a weekend even after a year of Covid-19. Give some tips to the valet people that park your car.  This restaurant serve dim-sum and dinner. Inside looks nice and clean.  I give them a 5 star for their service and I will definitely come back and I recommend coming here to eat if you are Cantonese.

I know we got here a bit late. They ran out of a lot of items for dim sum. However, my average rating is because only 1 out of the 8 dishes we did receive actually came out hot. Everything else was room temp. It was unfortunate.

Busy place and fast service. 
They have dim sum and a la carte dishes.
It was hard to find a parking place.
The dishes we orders were good.
One of my family's favorite banquet restaurants for the chinese holidays with private rooms. Great dim sums choices for lunch and brunch.
Terrible service. Waiters were extremely rude. Similar foods and be find else where with a much better experience. Will not come again

I passed by this restaurant about a million times when I exit the LIE, making the right turn onto Main Street to go to Flushing but I've never gotten to try it until today. The place that used to open early where I get dim sum from closed down and all the places by me opens at 11. I noticed a few weeks ago, ppl were coming out with bags of takeout from here early in the morning so I called to ask for their dim sum takeout hours and they said 7:30-4. Wow, that's early! If you're craving dim sum for breakfast, you should come here. 

I got 10 different dim sum dishes from here and they were all surprisingly good! I actually like their dim sum better than Northern Manor. It's less saucy and doesn't taste as heavy. Not to mention, the portions are bigger and the quality seems better. The service wasn't so great but what do you expect from a super busy dim sum place? My order was correct, ready in 20 minutes and everything was good, that's all that matters. There's a small parking lot in the back and valet up front. I'll definitely be back soon!

Everything we ordered from the dim sum  menu was really flavorful but they do need to step it up on their service. The use of plastic utensils, paper plates and cups just made me sad, it just didn't give me the full dim sum experience. Valet parking makes it so convenient. Price and the quantity is another reason for me to return.

Came here with my bf on labor day weekend at around 10:30AM and got seated right away surprisingly. You have to order by circling on a menu what you would like. There are barely any carts going around, probably due to covid. All the food was pretty fresh and tasty. The congee however was disappointing, as they did not include any thousand year old eggs. Some staples that were yummy were the pork spareribs, shrimp rice rolls, beef rice rolls, deep fried dough stick rice rolls, shumai, and egg tarts. The rice rolls were nice and chewy, thick and a good portion overall. Definitely super filling! Would come again.

Hello,I like to share my experience going for dinner with a friend on September 18-21. This restaurant look very nice  and expensive. We did not have reservations but the restaurant is very large so the hostess give a table for two,but we can tell she was no very please. One of the negatives is that like 90% of the staff don't speak any English, I'm an immigrant, but I thing that is important to be able to speak with your customers.second my friend notice that they serve our food in paper plates also de water and the coffee, but we noticed that all the tables had very nice table plates and silverware.Also we noticed that they want us to leave fast. The food was ok. My friend fell so uncomfortable that she wanted to leave,and when we ask a question they did not understand.I complain on a very nice way, but they say. We don't speak English. Also a very expensive, we paid full price for the food, but I feel that they treat us like we where second class citizens. My friend is a African American,and I'm from Latin America. I will like to have my money back ! 
We where so uncomfortable that we take the food to go .

A lot of variety dim sum. You order from a list . Prices reasonable.  The only thing is that while your food will come out quickly it's because everything that I ordered is ready to eat in carts at the back so basically they just remove it from the carts and bring it to you .  a bit lukewarm.
Taro dumplings big and filling was nice.  
Sponge cake was good. 
chive dumpling pan fried was also good
We always enjoy the food here. The tableware is now all paper products so it's kind of odd during a sit down meal but the quality we still enjoyed.

We leave not to far away, we passed by here many times. Why is it the first time we eat here, G-d only knows.
It's a very big donning hall, with valet parking and nearby street parking if you'd wish. We were seated right away.
We ordered from the dimsum menu which held a good variety. Every thing was delicious. Two items were almost cold because they don't have the cart service back yet (next week, we were told). It wasn't an issues, they took it back abs returned it very hot.
Service was immaculate, attentive, and welcoming. Our server was very sweet. 
We saw locals ordering non-Dimsum items that also looked delicious and we promised ourselves to be back for both dimsum cart service and dinner for non-dimsum items, like the Singapore noodles that looked amazing on other tables and a very nice portion.
Today was the first time dining here since pre pandemic and it was great. Prices are reasonable as it went up almost everywhere else but the quality and portions are good.

Ate in and did take out recently. Food hit the spot both times! When I ate in with my family, they provided a sheet where you just check off what dishes you want. Everything's in Chinese (not sure if they have an English version). Most of the food comes out at once and everything was amazinnggg. When I went to pick up takeout, I noticed the restaurant started having more aunties pushing the carts so I can't wait to go back to get the full dim sum experience again! 

As for service, don't be expecting too much, especially if you can't speak fluent Chinese. I also recommend bringing cash because they charge tax if you pay with credit card.

Came here with my parents, so we knew what we gona order before coming. Food are delicious, during weekdays, middle plates are the same price as big plates, so make sure you know what to get. I was really impressed by their Liusha bao, it was very delicious, unfortunately too slow to capture before it went in to my stomach.

It's been a long while since I eat in a legit Chinese dim sum restaurant. The building itself screams authentic Chinese from the outside and once you walk in, the decor, the setup, the music, everything just confirms it. Growing up, this is the kind of Chinese dim sum place I'm used to--large dining halls with round tables, atmosphere is loud as everyone is talking, we got served hot tea by the teapot, dim sum carts swirling around, the staffs in blazers/suits (everybody speaks Mandarin, but some staffs can accomodate English too), and a lot of the guests are eldery Asian. It's personally very nostalgic to me. Moreover, since I lived in the US, it's not very often I came across these places. They have a huge parking lot and it must be by valet ($3) as the parking lot gets jam-packed in no time, especially on Saturday morning since dim sum really is the epitome of Chinese brunch.
Recommended menu: 
- hakau (shrimp dumpling, they're huge and the skin is thin and nicely chewy)
- chicken feet (I know this one sounds bizzare, it's a love or hate kind of thing, but I personally love it)
- deep-fried shrimp cheong fun (it's not the same with shrimp cheong fun. The deep-fried one is so nice because it squidgier, fatter (not fatty, but i mean the shrimp is really huge and chunky), and had a crispy texture
- egg yolk bun (chinese white bun with runny fillings made of salted egg yolk, it's sweet but salty, trust me it's delicious)
- pan-fried water chestnut jelly (this is actually my first time trying but it's surprisingly good! lightly sweet, somewhat chewy, very fragrant, and the chestnut chunks adds a really nice layer of texture)
- black sesame roll (this is like steamed rice roll with black sesame, served cold, it has a slightly chewy texture and again, surprisingly very delicious)
Other things I tried included siew mai, taro cake, coconut pudding, fish ball. Overall, I think the food is really good. We had 12 portions total and the price is pretty reasonable. Service is good as well. Definitely not a bad dim sum place to go.

After the ways that Chinatown has changed, its not that easy to find cheap good dimsum in new york anymore. Long gone are the days of 2 dollar dimsum orders and now you're easily looking at 3-5 dollars especially outside of chinatown. In the hunt for an easily accessible(i.e. not flushing no parking), and solid dimsum we decided to try this place. I love the fact that they have a separate section for takeout orders/bakery. They also do have a parking lot so that was quite nice too; a stark contrast to downtown flushing. In any case, we had all the standard orders, beef rice roll, shrimp rice roll, siu mai and steamed cha siu baos. To my amazement each and everyone tasted exactly as it should; even the soy sauce had the right amount of salt and sweetness. The women working were also quite nice dealing with my messed up chinese. My one complaint is that when I went to purchase I paid whatever they said but I read the receipt and it said holiday pricing. Obviously there were no signs stating there was holiday pricing not to mention that it was the saturday after thanksgiving. I'll definitely try it again and see how much more it costs on holidays. Not sure why there are so many poor reviews here but this place checks almost all the boxes.

Great spot for classic dim sum and wedding banquets. They have all the classic Cantonese dishes, lobster noodles, shrimps, hargow, rice noodles are some of my favorites here. The shrimps have a nice bouncy texture and extremely fresh.
I ordered a 5 in 1 app platter and what a waste of money. We could not finish half of it.

New Lake Pavilion has been the go-to dim sum spot with my Yelp Elite friends. Our experience here has been good every time. We came here yesterday and reserved the private room in advance. There was a minimum $300 dining in the private room, but we missed the cut-off by about $50 and the manager was nice enough not to penalize us for not eating $300 worth of food.

We ordered the typical dim sum dishes (e.g. hargow, siu mai, chicken feet, and etc) and everything tasted delicious. I remember that I had their Despicable Me minion buns a few years ago and it was really good but we didn't order it yesterday.

It's easy to get here by bus or you can drive here and find street parking. They also have a parking lot here as well.

Really love the old school method of dim sum where the older CHinese ladies push around these  metal carts and scream out the names of the food they have in their carts in Cantonese. Their enthusiasm to sell or push off as many items to you can be taken As over offensive to borderline annoying at some point but they are doing their jobs. 

Food 5 stars 
The food here is great. Lots of unique items and the food tasted good. They even have a pineapple bun with egg yolk filling that sells out quickly so if you see it, make sure to grab it. 

Hygiene 1 star
I would say dirty cups and plates at these venues is normal, but then I found a hair sticking to the side of my tea cup. It was kind of gross when I found another hair stuck inside the beef tendon. Just make sure you look carefully before you bite down on any food!

First pushcart dim sum I've had in 15 years! You know they keep it traditional. I came with a friend who ordered/maneuvered everything, which made life easy for me, as my Chinese is not great. We ended up with:  

Meatballs -- big & juicy mmm lol
Tripe -- rather chewy which I didn't love
Shrimp shumai -- yum
Veggie dumpling -- also yum
Chashu buns -- didn't eat any myself but they were available and looked decent!
This colder dumpling with fried/breaded shrimp inside and sauce on top -- no clue what this was called but it was quite tasty!!!
Zhongzi lookin wrapped rice -- surprisingly flavorful filled rice

All of these dishes we asked for straight from the carts. The employees will definitely push you to try a bunch of items, but you gotta stand your ground lol. That's just the culture, and it made for a fun dining experience you don't get every day. There was a bunch of other items; we didn't even bother checking out the dessert cart bc we were so full! And there's a Chinese bakery connected to the restaurant for easy access.

No clue what the price point is bc my friend paid for our meal, how RUDE of her!

This is one of the few dim sum places still open for sit down service. They now have carts coming around during tea time.  You used to have to order by checking items off a list. (They are trying to come out of Covid.) They created a few new dishes for you to try/buy.  It's a variation of traditional items they have.  But the usual dim sum items are still available.  They have an amazing dinner menu And Take out too!  It's a little pricey but worth the splurge.

We were 5.  Everyone seemed to like the food. Some dim sum were better than others, but nothing was below average.  We got har gow, shu mai,  beef rice noodle, rice noodle with cruller, ribs in black bean sauce, chicken feet, choy sum, salt n pepper squid, crispy HK style noodles, sticky rice, shrimp paste in shishito pepper, steamed dumpling, pork bun pastry, and probably a few more that I forget.  Tea (2 kinds) was always promptly refilled, condiments had to be requested twice. fresh plates were supplied upon request.  The bill was $175 including a very generous $50 cash tip; I guess prices were fair not knowing breakdown.  Bathrooms accessible and clean enough.  Masking was not practiced, but each group got their own table.  Free valet parking.  We went Sunday around noon and were seated in 10 minutes.

Ordered the Chinese New Year eve dinner at this place, somewhat disappointing. When we placed the order, we told them that we would be picking up at 4:30pm. When we got there at 4:45pm to pick up, our order wasn't ready. There was a long line waiting in front of us and ended up we had to wait for another 30 minutes to pick up our order. The food was too salty. The duck was very dry and the skin was chewy. The shrimps seemed frozen shrimp and the meat did not taste fresh at all. The chicken was okay. Only the first layer was put together nicely, there were lots of food placed randomly in the lower layers. The parking in the front of the restaurant should be convenient for the customers, but it was not. People just dropped their car in the middle of the narrow driveway there and ran inside to pick up their orders. Ended up all the cars behind were stuck due to that inconsiderate customer leaving his car out there.

If you go in exactly at 9Am when it just open there is barely anyone there.   Foods aren't as great as before, however I noticed the cost more than before.   If you pay less tip they will ask for more.    Suggestion come after 9:30-10 because they don't start pushing the egg tarts and pastry until later on.

We happen to be in the area & since we wanted to grab some food we figured this was our best option. 
Came in & were seated right away , huge menu .. drinks we had Iced tea & soda along with the hot tea they provide, good hot tea. 
we simply just wanted some "regular" Chinese food we got Shrimp fried rice , Lemon Chicken & Pork lo mein, 
wish someone had warned us on the portion size , wow those 3 dishes could literally feed 3-4 people no lie , check out my pics! 
Pork Lo mein was very good, great taste to the meat & noodles, Shrimp fried was good as well but the winner for me was the Lemon chicken , little strips of chicken fried yes but did not really taste like they were fried? some seriously light batter they use or at least that's the way it taste chicken was delicious great on it's own very good when added to the rice. 
Needless to say we had a ton of leftovers. 
Decent looking place inside , odd when u walk in & u see all the seafood tanks but I guess this certainly provides some fresh seafood. 
Service was good , high prices but they give u very generous portions, we enjoyed our meal.

Love coming here but make sure you get here before 1:30. It seems everything is sold out or service is very mediocre past that. We waited almost 15 minutes till someone came to us and another 10 for the dim sum carts. Normally we get service within 3-5 minutes. Everything seemed to be sold out or cold. I also didn't see my normal selection. But overall I love their food and the quality.

Haven't visited here in a few years.  Free valet park in the back. Just pay at least $3 tips as you pick up your car.   
We went on a Sunday 1:00 pm.  Waited for only 10 min for a table.  Good customer service.  We were served tea right away and dirty dishes were taken away promptly.   
Price is market price.   They have the basic dim sum and a few own creations.   Overall the food was good. Only complain was the beef spare ribs was chewy.   
Free WiFi but it didn't work until half of the customers left.   
Overall we had good experience.  Will return.

Great dim sum place and family dinner place. My family has been loyal to them since their first location in the heart of flushing. Love that you can place a dim sum order separate from their dining area. 

I ordered a Poon Choy for an event and wasn't a big fan at all. I'll give it to them that it was filled with a lot of different things but not my cup of tea! Baby roast pig was good, it had a lot of meat in it and it wasn't just all crunchy skin.

Dim Sum is very busy on weekends/holidays. I called in my order 30mins prior to arrival and still waited another 10-15mins. The dim sum is just ok. Nothing spectacular with all the usual traditional dishes. The location is very convenient, right off the highway. There's a few municipal meters in the front and valet parking in the back.
Newly renovated restaurant.  Spacious and great for a lot of guests.  Parking in the back of the restaurant.

I've been going here for years and I've never had such terrible service until today. I understand it's busy, crowded and people are waiting, but there is no need to be rushed out of there the way I was today. 

First of all, the service was extremely rude especially the ones cleaning up the table. We were trying to remove the stroller from in between my table and the other table in which the man sitting wouldn't move his chair so the employee was yelling at US to "STOP!!" as they aggressively pushed the stroller away and then our table to the side towards my mother who was trying to get out of her seat at the same time and almost ran over her foot. We weren't trying to cause any trouble, but the way they treated us was so unwelcoming.

Secondly, I was getting my bag and the man cleaning up the table said "TIP!" And when I gave him the cash he told me it wasn't enough and shoved the money back into my hand. When I gave him more he tossed it on the table so aggravated. They never mentioned to me that there was a fixed rate for the tip, and I wouldn't have minded if there was, but I was just caught off guard by the nasty attitude. 

They need to do better. A busy place shouldn't justify rude service.

New Lake Pavilion is my go-to dim sum and dinner spot. They also have free parking in the back, which is convenient. Because of their location, it does get really packed on weekends and holidays, so be sure to get there earlier if you don't like to wait. 

Their food is great and you can always depend on them to satisfy your Cantonese food cravings. Some of my go-tos for dim sum are spare ribs, shrimp rice rolls, shu mai, and chicken feet. For dinner options, they have so much variety, but my favorites would have to be walnut shrimp, beef over pan fried noodles, jellyfish, stir fried scallops, and fried fish. 

Aside from having a long wait time when they get busy, this restaurant is a great place to eat at.

Dim sum was not bad. However, service was bad, so I won't go back. Shrimp ha cheung which comes with three pieces in a plate had only two. When we informed the floor personnel , he says we ate it! It was the first thing we ordered, and our plates were crystal clean, so it wax ridiculous what he said.

One of the better dim sum restaurant in Flushing area. All dishes are hot, fresh and savory.

Best part, no need venturing into downtown Flushing where parking is next to impossible.

Came here for dim sum on a Saturday afternoon. They have a parking lot which someone parks your car for you. However I was able to find treet parking nearby. Medium dim sum plate (like pork bun) was $4.50 and large dim sum plate (like shu mai and shrimp rice roll) was $5.25. We also got their lobster promo  which came with either 1 or 2 lobsters and a choice of noodle. We opted for 2 lobsters with pan fried noodles which was very good. 

They take credit card, Mastercard or Visa no Amex. Checking on our bill, they did over charge on tax (by 8 cents, maybe to make the bill an even amount) which is why you should always check your receipts.

I'd been wanting to go for a dim sum here the longest time, finally...today is the day!

Even though there was a long wait as big crowd  is lined up  by the door on our arrival , it did not stop us in staying as the lines anyway was moving  fast. Little didn't we know that it's already our turn after few minutes. 

Luckily seated away from many. My friend  still not comfortable to be in outdoor setting with too much people. Servers were wearing masks as good sign of CDC compliance. Hand Sanitizers are available for use   

Upon seating, the famous complimentary hot  tea has been served.  Then in a split  seconds we were seeing the food carts  circling the newly seated tables like us. 

We started the most enjoyable part of dim sum, picking the bamboo tray filled with food that caught our attention. Honestly , they'd pricing is economically reasonable.  Each tray costs less than $6. For our group of 3, total trays of 8 is good enough to satisfy our cravings. 

The service is good, the food is delicious and the ambiance is a happy one . 

One star less for the wait. Otherwise would've perfect  5. 

There is a valet car service.
Attended a wedding reception dinner recently. Friendly staff, great types of food served. Limited parking, street parking, valet service available.

The dimsum was absolutely horrendous tasting. This is probably the worst food I've had in years. At least two dishes had rancid meat. Server was also very rude and denied anything could ever be wrong with their meats. 
Quality and taste has gone way downhill.

Authentic dimsum in flushing with parking! Rare to come by. This is our go to for family and friends gatherings. They have a lot of seatings. Especially if you come weekdays before 12. You will be seated right away. Weekend mornings before 12pm isn't bad either. 
All the carts makes their round every so often. You just get the small dishes that looks good to you. Those ladies who pushes carts are quick to give you dishes, so if you don't want it make sure you tell them no lol. 
Things to get are chicken feet, steamed small ribs pieces, spareribs and shrimp dumplings, these are some of their best dishes. Also love their fish paste with pepper and water chestnut dessert. 
Price point depends on how many dishes you get but Generally if you get really full, it's around 20/pp. really not bad in this economy.
Large banquet space that can accommodate large parties. Solid traditional Cantonese food.

This restaurant has gone downhill over the years. I went over Columbus Day weekend with some friends and I was embarrassed that  I recommended this place for their first Dim Sum experience. We waited 5 minutes to be seated which is unheard of if you are a good Dim Dum restaurant on a holiday weekend. The lines use to be out the doors and you would have to wait at least a half hour.  The restaurant itself was run down and the bathrooms were filthy. The plates and utensils were dirty and the flood is mediocre at best. With all the new restaurants opening downtown Flushing, if they do not step it up, I can't see them staying open much longer.
Very authentic dim sum, the food here is better than most of the dim sun restaurants in flushing, expect a long wait on weekends

I'm vegan and this place is still my favorite.  Best dim sum spot in Flushing.   Others will beg to differ but I love the professional crew and that bald guy in the front.  The pricing is fair.  There is valet parking.  Definitely come by this place and enjoy.   I used to be a meat eater and I would come here with my wife every week.

Solid dim sum spot

Me and the fam were craving sum dim and we hit up this spot. We were fortunate to be seated right away without a reservation on black fruday (although the line quickly built up after we were seated). They had all the classic fare and did it well - pork buns, shrimp dumplings, various breads, zhongzi, spare ribs, leak buns, and veggies. Surprisingly they had soup dumplings which were quite good. They were even served in individual tin foil cups which made them easier to handle without fear of ripping. The only thing that wasn't good were the turnip cakes which were a bit undercooked and not nearly crispy enough. Otherwise great dim sum. In true authentic fashion, the staff were not particularly friendly, especially the guy in charge of valet parking. But whatever, they know you will come for the food xD
Decent dim sum place but it gets crowded quickly, so be sure to go early to avoid long wait.

This place is pretty crowded on the weekends for the dim sum so expect to share a table if you are a small party. The atmosphere is pretty noisy but that's expected with the crowd and the size of the room. Overall, they had a large variety of food. Some dishes were slightly under seasoned but most were still delicious. Their pineapple buns and ube pig buns surprised me. I will definitely be getting those when I go back!

Great place for dim sum.
Valet parking lot on site at the back.
Walk up to the podium by the cashier to get a table or join the list.
Not too crowded on weekdays.
Servers will come around to give you tea, and offer dim sum from the carts.

Chicken feet are usually very soft at the top of each piece. 9/10

Various dumplings are all good 8/10

Beef rice roll wasn't really rolled but open on one side. 7/10

6 dishes was about $33

Recommend you go with someone fluent in Chinese to make ordering etc easier.

At the end of your meal, let them know you're done and take the check to the cashier.
They accept cash and credit.
Leave tips on the table in cash if possible.

Coming to Flushing is like an event to me. Only when occasionally I must go to the LIC. I always stop by at this place for their takeout dim sum. 

Today again it was like fighting a war at the takeout. I loved how those old ladies behind the counter talking to each other in Cantonese. I couldn't understand a word but I loved it. What the most impressive was their math talent! They worked faster than any high tech calculators! All you needed to do was to hand in your cash through a jail-like tiny window. No, they would NOT let you distrust on the numbers given to you to pay. Lol! Yes, you were welcome to feel like you were just a piece of meat lying on a cutting board to be tenderized, and then left with somewhat uncertainty and happiness. Seriously, those old ladies were all very confident business women. I love to watch how they handle every and each customer in an engrossing and immersing manner at a super compact space! 

Today's sensation was the pandam black/white sesame mini balls. The simple black sesame taste along with some magic rich flavor packed in those tiny bodies.  Not yet figured out what exact the flavor was like. 
All dim sum sizes were nice today. However I noticed that all bread bakeries looked sallow in the show case. Obviously, dim sum were the heart and soul of the day.
Very good! Came here with my family early because we know this place fills up fast. Was sat immediately. Had a wide a variety of dim sum and good service!

Great spot for dimsum. They have a parking lot but it can get crowded so park in the surrounding blocks. I love how they have a takeout area with all the various dim sum so you can take it to go. Plenty of space and large tables at the restaurant. Highlights are the private rooms for your big family or friend gatherings. Fresh variety of dimsum, love the har gow, shrimp rice rolls, and any of the buns. Ordering any of the noodles from the kitchen is good as well such as the chicken chow mein. Definitely will be back.

I will give it zero star if it is possible. I know it is busy, but why the waiter and waitress shouting at us.the valet parking man's face is so bad. The waiter assigned seats shouted us and looks like we are not customers but bugging for food.

We went at 1pm and the food tasted like they have b bc even cooked some time ago and have just been kept warm. 
We also bought big steam buns in the take out store which were quite good.

This is all my time favorite dim sum place in Flushing, Queens. Always come here either dine in with family or take out (I wish they deliver). This place gets really packed during any holidays or long weekend. So I always order take out to avoid the wait. On normal days, we would come here at around 11am/11:30am and have to wait prob 20-30mins for table. 

The restaurant is not that big and not very new but it is good for people who don't want to go all the way to Main Street for dim sum. I like the quality of their food even tho there aren't as many varieties compared to the ones in Flushing. My favorite is their egg tarts and "white snow bun" which has custard inside the bread! It's not too sweet and still
Crispy when we eat it at home. The eggs tarts here are one of the best. Some people might prefer cookie crust but I like the other style here. Yummy!

Came for Sunday dim sum and was surprised by the spacious interior and impressed with the variety of selections for dim sum! All tasted great except the turnip cake tasted a bit salty to me and wasn't sure if I liked it compared to other places. Since it's bigger, I sometimes had to go to the carts to get what I wanted which I don't mind but can see how others may not prefer it. The service was good like if I didn't see something on the cart, I asked one of the servers and they went out to find it for me and brought it to my table. They change/clean tables quickly so even if there is a line, it does move quick. We came around 9:30am and got seated right away and when we left around 11am it was getting busier. There's valet parking in the back but not really clear about parking fee, we tipped $5 and they didn't ask for more.

A new low for the food and service.  Our fried chicken came out a couple minutes from ordering COLD and dry.  Clearly it was prefried and sitting somewhere. We complained and they replaced the order.  Our Yee Mein noodles w mushrooms had a couple of slivers of mushrooms which was dug up like an archeological dig by the waiter when we complained.  He acted like the two slivers of mushrooms were perfectly satisfactory. On top of everything it was bland.  He refused to replace the noodles.  Beef chow fun was better at my local Chinese take out.  I hope I never come back here.

To be fair, we had takeout. 

Beef tripe radish mixto: bland & mushy
Ha-gow: mushy all around 
Ha-cheurng: shrimp overdone. Noodle, unremarkable
Fung-Jow: meh
Pai-gwuk: meh
Fried egg roll: meh

Highlights:
Giant sticky rice in banana leaves 
Fried taro 
Siew mai and salted egg buns were good enough
Fried cruller cheurng

This place was booming ppl lining in, out in haphazard design. They were able to get out takeout packaged and accurate in a phone order in 25 minutes which is quite a feat. Clearly something had to give for this type of volume. Sadly, it's quality but had we had this sitting down, it could've gone a lot better. But there r just too many really great dim sum 2 miles away and all over the city.

I downgraded my rating cause of the heavy crowds now, it's just crazy the wait AND the waiting area.  We came here this morning at 10:20 and the parking lot already had a line. We skedaddled and went to New Mulan instead which had open tables.  I returned in the afternoon to get takeout dim sum from the takeout section. The communication is difficult due to the covid barriers still up, and the cashier and person who packs your order need to have more efficient communication.  But they work nicely.  You just have to keep an eye on which person is packing your to-go order.  The cashier is a bit close to the servers so that space can get a bit claustrophobic. But their dim sum, while not cheap, is decent quality.  The corner parking on Main and HHE is a large reason i'm a regular takeout customer here.

Came here for Chinese New Year family dinner, and put together our own set menu, based around the roast suckling pig that we pre-ordered.  Food was excellent, plentiful, and cheap.  In addition to the pig (which was crisp, juicy, flavorful), we also ordered fried tofu, fried shrimp with walnuts, Peking fried pork chop, lobster Cantonese, roasted chicken, fried flounder, stir-fried pea shoots, fried rice, chicken pan-fried noodles.  All were excellent.  Plenty of leftovers for the rest of the week was a bonus.

I must confess, I went here twice in one weekend. Both times was take out. I really enjoyed the food. It was delicious and cheap. Yes, dim sum prices have gone up with inflation and honestly, with non-chinese people discovering it but the prices still remained ok here. You must understand, it is part of the experience for them to shout at you. Don't knock it. Cantonese culture is like that; I know, I grew up with that. You see similar things in other cultures too, where it seems like they are yelling at you but really, they are just speaking normally according to what they know. It helps to have someone who speaks Cantonese order it as they ladies do not know English well. The food was hot, fresh and came FAST. you literally order and the food is packaged for you at the same time so you will pay and get your order immediately after. They offer more variety if you call in vs what you order in the take out part of the restaurant. I am usually very picky about dim sum and this one passed my test. Could it be cleaner though? Probably but I choose to distance that in my mind!

We ate dim sum at this place today. Food was just average. But the worst part was the yee mein noodle with crab meat, which was mostly noodle. There were a few pieces of mushrooms in the noodle. But for crab meat, you would need a magnifying glass. A few tiny pieces mixed with the noodle. WTH?

Do have dimsum before 12pm on weekends, anytime after that you will have to wait about 20 minutes for a table.  Specially if you have large parties of 5 or more people.  Clearly parking is an issue, they have a parking lot but good luck, always packed.  Food is cery reliable, we had the rice crepes stuffed with beef and we also ordered the knes with shrimp.  Had the classic chicken feet, tripe, tofu skins with vegetables and chicken, taro piff with stuffed with savory beef, dimsum is always reliable, we had to wait about 10 minutes at 11:30am for a table of 4ppl.

Great place to get dim sum at!
Great variety!

Most likely a line during weekend brunch/dim sum hours!

In Flushing, a neighborhood known for its diverse and vibrant culinary scene, New Lake Pavilion stands out as a destination for Cantonese food lovers. The restaurant occupies a large space on Main Street. Inside, you'll find a lively and elegant dining room, where white tablecloths and fresh flowers contrast with the noise and bustle of carts laden with dim sum.

The restaurant also boasts an impressive selection of seafood dishes that are prepared with fresh ingredients from the tanks at the entrance. You can choose your own fish, lobster, crab, scallops or clams and have them cooked in various ways: steamed with ginger and scallions, fried with salt and pepper, braised with oyster sauce or stir-fried with noodles. The seafood is tender and flavorful, complemented by simple seasonings that let their natural sweetness shine.

New Lake Pavilion is not a place for quiet conversations or intimate dates. It's a place for celebrating life with good food and good company.

Extremely unhappy experience. Valet parking will charge you even if you park yourself. The guy claimed he doesn't work for the restaurant but it literally says restaurant parking. The dim sum cart ladies yelled at us in a group of 4 people while we had trouble understanding them because they marked an item before it was served. They did not care to make sure we understand. The food itself was mediocre and some are oily than average dim sum places. Highly NOT recommend. Come here if you just feel like giving money away to the "valet" guy who makes money for collecting car keys and not parking your car.
Interesting place. Service was good. Mostly Asian patrons so I thought the food would be better. Mediocre. Perhaps we didn't know what to order.

Lake Pavilion is a classic Cantonese-style restaurant that's been my family's go-to dim sum and dinner spot for many years. We dined here for a milestone birthday on a Saturday evening with about 8 large tables. We ordered about 10+ family style dishes per table and they tasted delicious. All the dishes came out in a reasonable time and was very fresh. My favorite items include the mayo shrimp, cold seafood sampler, deep fried tofu, and the seafood soup. I will be returning for dim sum in the future.

Been here many times before but today, worse service. Beginning of the service, I asked for an extra serving but lady asked how many people we had in the private room. I had to count and I'm like does it even matter, I know we need an extra setting PERIOD. I had 6 white people" (3 of the 6 white people were Indian) plus 8 Asians but lady dared asked how many people we had. We had 13 people with 13 chairs and you had 12 settings. I asked for one setting so give me one fking setting. Don't question it lady. The food was fine but the service is terrible. We spent over $1,000 and the service was horrendous. They didn't change plates til we finished food. Go somewhere else if you have "white" people in your party. Oh yes, they said "they don't know how to eat the fish head (soup)" in Chinese plus other racial comments. Save your money and go somewhere else.
Dim Sum is good with varieties. The parking lot creates an convenient for weekend enjoyment.

Went during lunchtime on a holiday with a large party and was seated relatively quickly, even though it was busy! The dim sum dishes were delicious and came out timely, and staff worked quickly but was also accommodating considering how hectic dimsum usually is. Parking is in a small valet lot, but wasn't a hassle. Great place!

Very good dimsum at lunch. There's a lot of food to choose from. The place is elegant, the chairs are covered with cloth. There's parking at the back. Avoid going on weekends, there's a long wait No dimsum in the evening .

Very good food,big portion , family style, good service.
A little pricey , not inexpensive,  but they give you bigger portions as I mentioned. I will be going back soon as I enjoyed the food very much.

This place is known for their dimsums in the morning but it is often over crowded. The parking lot is valet but you can never find space. Street parking.. forget about it unless you park 5 blocks away or near by and risk your car being scratched. 

We came here for dinner. The food is just okay. Sweet and sour pork was covered in dough. Combination Cold Cut Platter was different but just okay. Expensive food for just okay food. 

The manager (bald headed guy) is rude. Feels like he's always in a bad mood or a bomb that's about to burst. 

Moral of the story: just okay.
Love it here we come often for dimsum!!! Very good authentic dimsum very nice people great food

We came on a Friday afternoon and the place was busy but we didn't wait too long to be seated. The restaurant offers complimentary valet parking, which is a nice perk given the location. Food and service was subpar and wasn't anything special compared to other dim sum places around the area.

Just came from dimsum over there  my friend knows a few workers there  So the services was exceptional !  Besides Dimsum we also had a dish called Country Style Chow fun with Salted fish  It was out of this world!!  Fantastically delicious..

The decor is ornate in cheesy Chinese fashion (not exactly bad, it's a thing!). The red tablecloths and napkins feel a little fancy. Good is quite good. Standard Cantonese fare executed well. There is parking in the back, but prepare for a wait to get your car out when it fills up. Place was hopping on a Saturday night.

Foods were not very fresh and the servers were super pushy. They wanted us to buy everything. It was not a good experience dining there, especially there are so many good Chinese restaurants in flushing.

Servers were pleasant enough. Food was mediocre. We ordered 5 dishes so had a sampling of Different things. Nothing was memorable. Most of the food was greasy. Not sure what happened with the kitchen. Woman i was with was so excited about going here as her experience in the past was that it was phenomenal. No so anymore. By the way, many reviewers refer to dim sum. The night we were there (mid week) there was no dim sum. Call ahead.

This used to be the Go To place for dim-sum with good service. Not anymore. Granted, I was there for a family dinner 2 days ago. Almost all dishes tasted overnight-ish (Peking Duck, chicken), not fresh!  The fruit platter that came at the end included bad tasting cantaloupes!  The Red bean soup was over sweetened and not sure it's eatable.
The waitress who served us was unfriendly and impatient, she was almost "throwing" the dishes onto the table... 
The place smelled like cigarette smoke when I first walked in, carpet was worn out, bathroom was unclean. Do not recommend this place and will not go there again.

Everything is amazing!! The best food in town.. The roasted duck is amazing which is my personal favorite! I had a birthday party here for my son the food was great & the service was great also. It's a large restaurant perfect for family or group gatherings!

Food (5/5): Delicious dim sum with quite good options. We got rice rolls, shu Mai, meatballs, and other dim sum. Almost all the dim sum we got were delicious.

Service (3/5): We had a 20 minute wait to get a table for 6. They set table when we got seated. They didn't check up on us frequently and asking for chili or water requires effort to get their attention or to stand up and look for someone. The carts took a bit to come to us.

Ambiance (3/5): Very busy dim sum restaurant with lots of people. It will be quite loud and bustling. There are plenty of seats and it is quite spacious. The place appears mostly clean.
Probably the best roast pork buns around, since they closed Hop Shing in NYC on Chatham Square. This is way more authentic than Mei Lai Wah without the long lines and chunks of fat!

This is a pretty popular place for dimsum. We've been here for dimsum, dinner and also a banquet. So now I feel like I am somewhat qualified to give it an overall rating. 

As for dimsum, they are one of the better ones in Flushing. Might not be the top, but they are up there. They supply much of the traditional dimsum, which in general are made well. The carts are supposed to roll through the restaurant so that everyone gets an opportunity to get something from the cart. But very often, the carts stay idle or move at several feet per 10-15 minutes, due to the overwhelming requests or many questions from the nearby patrons. I feel like they need 2-3 carts which carry the same dishes rather than just 1. Service can also be a little better. Manager likes to rush people.

As for dinner & banquet, I will just group them together since banquet dishes are really 1.5 to 2X of a dinner order. Overall the dishes are pretty decent, especially the traditional dishes.
