The rest which are supposed to be more creative or "fancy" are OK. The "fancy" dishes I feel are unecessary and doesn't really add to the dish. For example, there is a traditional deep fried crispy skin chicken which they take and "reinvent". They really just take the skin off the chicken, then ground the chicken and whip it into a paste or dace. They they layer chicken dace, shrimp dace, cook it and then you still get the crispy chicken skin on top, then yet another layer of semi candied almond slices. Then they put it back together to form the shape of a chopped chicken on a plate. When you take a bite, I guess it's supposed to have a nice snap from the shrimp and then a bit of crunch from the almond, but then it doesn't. I guess it's about texture? I had a piece and a half and said, "meh". In any case, I would rather have the traditional crispy skin chicken instead. I would have chomped down several pieces, heck an entire chicken leg for that matter. 

So the conclusion... Dim sum all the way!! Dinner, stick with traditional dishes, you can't lose. No need to pay $$$$$ for the "fancy" stuff.

Slow service. Taste of the food are average level in the area. But the worst part, server told us you didn't leave enough gratuity for their service which i don't think it is worth it. Plus How dare are you that telling customer you have to tip more.
Hustle of bustle of Chinese big group meet ups. Recommend for large parties. The dishes are huge. Servers are very nice, gets work done, fast and efficient.

Super packed every time I come. If you come during weekends, be sure to come SUPER early as the wait typically takes a long time. They have valet parking in the back. Don't expect much from the service as well, like any dim sum places, since they're so packed. Food is pretty good every time we come. One of the top ones out of most of the dim sum I've had. They are also the only one ik that sells "gum-sa-cheung" which usually gets sold out real quick once it's out. The siu mai have also been getting really good there recently and they're huge. It's a very open space with a lot of tables and seatings, so not much space between tables but food is good and never had a bad experience with the food.
Great Peking duck! Soup dumplings were fantastic.  Service was ok, and short ribs were ok.

Dimsum is fine.  Sometimes the noodles are too salty.  The food is mostly good. Depending on manager, it can be a bad experience if you are a little claustrophobic.   If the bald man manager seats you, make sure you avoid the sectioned off back half of the room. Not sure why but the far back room almost sent me running from the place literally.   The air is stuffy and the ac might not be on.   I had to breathe to get me through dimsum.  Not exactly making my family want to come anymore.

Came here for dim sum on a Sunday afternoon, take a number and wait to be called. There is valet parking but some of us had to find parking on the streets. 

Dim sum carts were coming around regularly, they have a good variety. 

Prices are better here than in Manhattan Chinatown. Will be back!

Great spot for dimsum. Lots of variety and fresh dimsum (yay ladies in carts!). They have a large parking lot that is double, triple parked with valet. So we ended up street parking in the residential area and walking. Huge space with lots of tables. They have private rooms if you have a larger party. When we were about to leave, they were putting up beautiful Chinese panels - probably to block out half of the space for a wedding (I think).

Stopped by with family on a random Thursday evening recently with guests from out of town. There was virtually no one in the dining room which was great. We had plentiful parking spots to choose from and was one of 5 tables dining in. Unfortunately the waiter either did a bait and switch or really didn't know his inventory. He advertised razor clams but then we swapped since they discovered they didn't have any. The clams dish was fresh and tasty and large. Then we ordered a fresh fish to be done with soup and also stir fried and he came back and said that particular fish was not available but here are the other options...we then asked for squab and he said no you need to pre-order that but we have pigeon. he suggested ordering the number of guests we had and when the dish came out I was embarrassed. they were so meatless and just was not enough especially if someone wanted seconds. I believe they also charged us for the white rice which I find tacky. its not the price it's the principle. at least for Chinese family style places that I typically dine in, they include the rice, as much as you want. they did bring out red bean dessert and fruit so that was a nice touch because many places don't do both anymore. I'm not fluent in reading Chinese when the bill came so lord even knows what I was charged for each dish. overall an ok experience with family / out of towners.

My favorite dim sum place of all-time! While they are often very busy on weekends and may have long wait times, I would say it is worth the wait. There is a HUGE selection of dim sum from all your classics (har gow, siu mai, chicken feet, cheong fun, beef tripe) to more contemporary and all the different steamed and baked buns (roasted bbq pork bun, pineapple bun, Snow White bun). I love their lo mai gai (steamed lotus sticky rice) that is seasoned so wonderfully with lots of sauce and filling. My favorite bun would have to be their salted egg yolk steamed bun that oozes as soon as you take a bit. The perfect amount of sweet and savory. Their traditional malay guo (steamed Malaysian cake) is incredibly soft, pillowy, and fluffy, with the perfect amount of sweetness. Don't forget about their desserts too! Flaky, buttery egg tarts, coconut pudding, silken tofu, chrysanthemum pudding, and more. Just the vast variety amazes me. And of course, there are also the made-to order dishes too like stir-fried veggies, noodles, rice, meats, and seafood.
Dim sum is the best around. Really authentic and delicious. Regular menu is also outstanding.

Today, at about 2:30pm, I bought take-out from their take-out counter and noticed their beef cheung fun (a/k/a rice rolls a/k/a noodle rolls) had significantly thicker skin than in the past, way below standard.  Does this match anyone else's recent experience?  If so, I'd hazard to guess they had lost their main dim sum chef or had gotten lazy.  Neither one is a good sign.  

Also the 1 order of spring rolls were all vegetarian, as opposed to having little bits of pork inside.  I wasn't told they were all vegetarian and that should have been made clear by the sign or told to me.

Granted, it's later in the day, but 2:30pm is not all that late.

My friend recommended this restaurant for dim sum and I've been wanting to try for ages but I couldn't help but worry about the potential communication challenges. To my pleasant surprise, my dining experience at New Lake turned out to be quite exceptional. 

Upon entering, my family and I were immediately seated and the push cart ladies surrounded us at once. It definitely felt overwhelming due to the language barrier and the vast array of food offered that we were unfamiliar with. However, the push cart ladies were friendly and accommodating. One had even offered us a dim sum menu with visuals so the table could order food confidently and without miscommunication. It never seemed like they avoided our table after knowing that we couldn't speak the language. Instead, they kept coming by and offering us different dishes to try. One of the ladies even went out of her way to find me the pineapple roast pork bun that I had asked if she had in her cart. Superb service!   

My family ordered both from the dim sum carts and the extensive menu that had the typical meat, seafood, noodles, and rice dishes. We ordered:
- young chow fried rice (6/10): not the most flavorful, felt like it was missing something but it had lots of shrimp which was nice 
- salt & pepper pork chops (6/10): very salty, they were very generous with the seasoning   
- 1/2 crispy fried chicken (7/10):  my mom's favorite cause of the crispy skin but for me it was average at best
- Pork Chops Peking Style (sweet & sour) (8/10): the sauce really made the dish taste so good, prefer this dish over the salt & pepper pork chops. 
- Shanghai soup dumplings (9/10): the soup was very tasty and it didn't burst when I picked it up
- Sesame balls (10/10): I think it was a green tea (?) black sesame ball. My dad really liked it and said it was "not too sweet", which is the ultimate compliment that an Asian can give a dessert
- Portuguese egg tarts (10/10): so flaky and the custard wasn't too sweet but definitely satisfied my sweet tooth after a great meal 
- eggplant stuffed shrimp (8.5/10): unexpected dish of the day that everyone liked at the table 

The portions were impressively large - we left with full stomachs and delicious leftovers. But I definitely prefer ordering from the dim sum carts and getting the buns, pastries, and steamed dumplings. Highly recommend getting the roast pork buns, pineapple roasted pork buns, sesame balls, and Portuguese egg tarts. 

Definitely give this place a try whether you're a dim sum aficionado or a first-timer, New Lake Pavilion promises an unforgettable experience.

We have been here so often and it's always terrific. My husband's 70th birthday party was there this weekend and the staff went above and beyond.  Sam, who was in charge of the event, sent me a printed menu the day I made the arrangements.  He got back to me immediately every time I contacted him and was always one step ahead.  The service was flawless and the staff divided leftovers for our party guests to take home. They were amazing. Can't imagine a more flawless venue   Thanks to all of there who did an outstanding job. By the way, the food was terrific as usual.

This is a small mom and pop dim sum place. The classics are there and fresh as they only have 1 cart. The flavor is a bit lacking in salt, prob why i see every table with a bottle of soy sauce lol. Service was nice, would go back since it closer than the other dim sum place and no wait.

Lake Pavilion has always been our Go To Cantonese restaurant - from tea, dimsum and main dishes.  You'll never go wrong if you are looking for an authentic, no- after taste Cantonese food, this is the place!  The taste, texture and presentation is always consistent. And also, much, much cleaner compared to other Chinese restaurants ; even their toilet. The service is fast and waiters know how to speak english a little bit. The ambience is conducive to eating with chinese decorative colors.
Came here because I was looking for dim sum place with parking. No regrets! Food was good, prices were quite reasonable. Would definitely go back.
Everything about this place is kool! Great food and great service! The place was empty and we enjoyed it that way! Like I had rented it out for my husband's birthday! Perfect.

Food is ok, but the service is really bad, I would put no star but I can't post my feedback without a minimum. The waitress had an attitude to begin with. I asked if they can make the plain rice rolls for my kids, she responed "what do you want?" was such a "b" word!! but ok, maybe it's busy. I saw a bag on one of the empty chair on my table, I told her about it and she just said its hers, she forgot about it ... no thank you or appreciation ... if I knew it was hers, I would have just tossed it under the table instead of being nice about it.

My friend knows one of the managers and he gave us the waiver on the tea surcharge ... yes, they charge $1.50 per person for tea. When I got the bill, it was subtotal $131 + $11 tax = $142. I took my phone and did 15% on $131 and I left a tip of $22. The waitress demanded I give more. I asked why? I gave you more than 15%. she said I didn't give the minimum tip from the $142. I argued, when do we pay tip on taxes?? she then say they didnt charge the tea surcharge so I should give them more tip. Really? so if I was charged the $1.50 /person then can I leave lesser tip?? I didnt know there was a minimum gratuity law in nyc.

This is not the first time where their waitresses demand more tips from customers not sure if the restaurant management knows about this but I don't think they care either ... seems like a gold digger corporation. Never going back.

Watched Bon Appetite's YouTube with Lucas Sin's review of this restaurant. He and chef Eric Sze literally ate everything dim sum and gave very good comments and recommendations. We ate a few of their likes and it's so delicious!!! Unfortunately, not everything they ate was available when we went. The Malaysian steamed cake was the best! It's not gummy like many dim sum places. So happy to discover this restaurant in Flushing. They have valet parking in the back of the restaurant. Valet is free, just tip.  
The 1 thing to comment is they need to remodel their restrooms badly!

Food was excellent, good service and ambiance was little too bright.  Dimming the lights would be nice!! Highly recommended for anyone!  Also private party dining rooms available for celebrations of all kinds!!

FYI, this place offers high end seafood dishes!! Great dim sum by day,  but even better seafood restaurant by night!! Please enjoy..

Every dim sum place does things a little bit differently and that's what we felt here with some of their items. All of the standard items were really good but just the occasional difference in ingredient was the only reason why we didn't think it was amazingly good. One of the other thing that marked it down was that their salted egg bun was not runny and cooled off a bit. I feel that this bun is an indicator of a good dim sum place because not all places will serve it and not all places will have it good. 

The plus is that they do cart style which is amazing and really elevates the dim sum experience! Surprisingly on a weekday they still had a good amount of people! 

Overall, it was really good and not expensive as you would get it in the city and I would definitely come back again!

Christmas dim sum with my boyfriend and my sister. Went there super early [8:40am to be exact] we were the ONLY ones there, but within mins it started to fill up with large groups.  Luckily we got there super early with a good seats. 

When we left around 10am there was a huge line and the parking lot was bumper to bumper. 

Here's the damage for today
- Steam Beef Balls
- Chicken feet 
- Steam spare ribs 
- Black pepper beef ribs 
- Century egg pork congee 2x
- Stuffed eggplants with shrimp 
- Coconut pudding 
- Sticky rice wrapped with lotus leaves 
- Cha Guo 2x
- Beef Cheung fun 2x 
- Pork peanuts Crystal dumplings 
- Fried Sticky rice 
- Bean Curd rolls pork fillings
Very busy today during our dim sum run! No surprise there though. The food never disappoints! No Wu Gok :(

I LOVE this places dim sum and one of the best I have had in my life.  I grew up with dim sum in  Chinatown in Manhattan, San Francisci, Hong Kong,  Honolulu....  

My dear friend who is from Hong Kong but has lived in flushing for a half century took me to this place first time a year ago. I think this speaks everything. 

Pls see the pictures and videos.  Everything was just delicious. I uploaded on Instagram, too. 

I don't know about services because they are very attentive as my friend is a king customer there (lol).

Good spot to stop in for dim sum. Very accessible by car/ bus. Located right along Horace Harding Expressway; away from the hustle & bustle of Main St. flushing. Has a few parking spots up front, & a nice parking lot in the back. Can be packed on holidays. Service is decent. Decor is a little outdated.

The front desk lady is very rude and very demanding on higher tips than an average 15%. Not to mention she doesn't greed well and say thank you after receiving money.  But, the food is great and definitely will come back

This is my second time here. Wanted to introduce dim sum to my friend without having to venture into Manhattan or Main Street, Flushing. Alas, this was a pretty good spot that had parking. We ended up using street parking since they charge you to use their parking lot. 
I was able to get a table for two surprisingly! So glad they had that option. It was traditional style dim sum, where there are non English speaking women that walk around with carts offering various dishes. I'm usually not comfortable with this set up unless I have my Asian friends with me who can translate. Fortunately, there was a menu available ! I got to try a number of dishes and my friend was very happy all of them. Few things I wished were different:
1) wish there was a flame under the teapot to keep it warm , since it got cold pretty quick 
2) they did not have the character egg custard buns and I received the plain ones . Not a big deal. But they are aesthetically pleasing so wish it was available!
3) I wish there was a non pork congee available. A LOT of the items have pork in it and I wish there was a vegetarian version of the same dishes. 
4) The receipt system is confusing. Every time you order something, they stamp it on a card (it's not in English either) and then the check is handwritten with nothing itemized. I wish it could be a bit more modern, so we could see all the items clearly listed and their prices like an actual receipt. They accept credit card so that's good. 

For the location and price point, I might come here again but I hope things change!

One of my favorite dim sum spots in queens. It does get really busy on weekends. So be prepared to wait, there is parking in the back but it does get packed. My favorite is the shrimp and beef noodle, shomai and tripe.

We come from Buffalo and love to grab dim sum here w our family who lives around the corner. We've been here many times. Today we came for lunch. Food was great, service was as it normally is. When we got the bill, my father in law set cash on the table for the tip and the waitress motioned for him to take it back and she said 'it's included'. We thought that was strange, but whatever. He went up and paid the bill. As we exited the front door, the same lady literally chased us out the door and made a scene about us not leaving a tip. We questioned her as to why she said it was included, she didn't answer. She told us how much money we 'had' to leave, and then demanded more on top of that. 
She was reminded of a few things:
She told us tip was included
Very unprofessional to make a scene like that
You don't chase customers
And you don't DEMAND tips
Tips are a representation of the service you received 
I have never in my life been chased out of a restaurant over literally $10!! If it was up to me, I would have told that woman to pound salt and walked away, leaving her empty handed. You don't treat customers like that. She should be ashamed and embarrassed of her behavior.

Came here on a weekend evening for dinner. It was busy but we didn't have to wait long for table. 
Service was not great. We thought the host that seated us was quite rude. The waitstaff was ok.
The food was decent. The portions were ok, definitely nothing to brag about. There are plenty of other Cantonese restaurants like this that we would probably prefer to go to. Thanks

So I came with a group of about 10 people for lunch a couple of days ago and was pretty happy with the food. The place reminded me of one of those Chinese wedding halls, food was delicious. It was the first time I ever had dim sum. My favorite dish was by far the fried chicken with scallions on top it was moist yet crunchy. Service was fast and people were nice the only thing was that they seemed to be a little pushy trying g to get us to get more dim sum. Price wise it was decent.
classic dim sum here. has many many options. also worth watching eric szes youtube video beforehand of all the options you could get
I love New Lake Pavillion. The dim sum is awesome! I often get take order there for my favorite dishes: salt and pepper pork chop, garlic pea shoots,  and beef chow fun.

As a native Queens lifelong resident I have many times passed New Lake Pavilion during my travels, but this is my first visit with my family for a Saturday March, 2024 brunch.  This large Chinese banquet hall restaurant is located at the peripheral south of Flushing upon the Long Island Expressway exit.  Ahh, nostalgia of growing up with large Chinese banquet halls in Manhattan for Dim Sum parlors of classic Cantonese cuisine and New Lake Pavilion stand their ground resisting progress and inflation, especially agflation.  The decor is beautiful with painting panels on the partition dividers and chandeliers adored the ceiling chandeliers adored the ceiling with mural painting Cherubs.  My foodie synopsis:

siu1 maai6/2 燒賣 - Pork and mushroom dumpling were well prepared, but the mushroom were too large and overpowered the dumpling.

zyu1 coeng4*2/4 fan2 豬腸粉 - Chee Cheong Fun rice noodle roll was very fresh, but the texture was too chewy from the thickness.

ngau4 juk6 coeng4*2 牛肉腸  Beef rice noodle roll rice roll, same as the other cheong fun, texture was too chewy from the thickness.

haa1 coeng4*2 蝦腸 蝦腸 Shrimp rice noodle roll, the same as the other cheong fun, texture was too chewy from the thickness.

haa1 gaau2 蝦 餃 - Shrimp dumplings was blooming with shrimp, less dumpling wrapping.

zan1 zyu1 gai1 - Sticky rice lotus wraps were good consistency.

mong4 gwo2 bou3 din1 芒果布甸 - Mango pudding was very lumpy like feta cheese and it was not mango juice.  This was truly disappointing.  It is one of my favorite dim sum desserts.  To further my despondent, there were no hang6 jan4 dau6 fu6 杏仁豆腐 almond pudding in the Dim Sum food carts.  The ladies pushing the food carts, thankfully, speak Cantonese and rather aggressive to sell the food.  Business card and take-out menu are available for grabs.

Food in any cultural cuisine is what brings people together as a community united. The Dim Sum is solid and I ate my fill.  Yum Cha, please! Our tea were refilled with hot water.  Facilities were decent and accessible without any stairs.  Customer service is average and somewhat attentive.  I finally managed to awake from being wracked with intense grief to get out into the world for food.

There is a small parking lot, but it quickly becomes very filled for full occupancy.  New Lake Pavilion is very accessible via public transit by MTA 7 train and MTA buses Q17; Q48; Q25; Q34; Q65; Q27; Q19; Q66; N20G; N20X; Q20A; Q20B; Q44-SBS; Q50; Q26; and Q12.

We came here for dinner and had a great experience. The food was delicious, the portions were huge, and the service was good. Normally we come here for dim sum/lunch and it is usually crazy and hectic, and the service during these busy times is pretty bad. However, tonight the restaurant was not packed and we had a great time. We will definitely come back for dinner on other occasions. My favorite item was the crispy Sea bass, and the Peking pork chop.

Booked a room at the restaurant for dinner for my sons first birthday. I booked my reservation with Sam. He was very responsive and helpful. He was able to send me the menu and make recommendations on what to order. 

The room was big and spacious. The staff was very attentive and they serve the food for everyone. We ordered 2 set menus. 1 seafood set for 10 people and 1 regular set for 8 people. We had about 16 people and that was way too much food. 

The food was all presentable but the taste was bland. There were not a lot of flavors. The food just tasted as it was downed in water and oil. The food is not really up to par but this place provide a private room and good service for special occasions.

I've been looking for a decent dim sum place in a neighborhood of Queens. Ever since Ping's closed and not wanting to wait 1-2 hours at Jing Fong over at Chinatown, I thought I give this establishment a try. Not sure why this place only get 3 stars on yelp, I really thought the options here are really optimal and authentic as it gets. On a side note, I used to pass this place all the time not knowing it's a yumcha spot, silly me. Everything is good, the ladies who push these carts were also kind and helpful although they speak very little to no English. Food is delicious and this restaurant is jam packed right from the get go. I came in today for a party of 2 earlier today around 1pm and there are long lines to get a table. We ordered 2x Har gao [shrimp dumpling], chicken feets [my favorite classic], shumai, pineapple pork buns, portuguese egg tarts,  congee thousand year old eggs and shrimp cheong fun. Lord have mercy, they have the best shrimp cheong fun [not sure if there is a light fried yu tiao mixed with rice dough and a whole lot shrimp but its the best of its kind. Their pineapple pork buns, not too sweet with the char shiu yet the dough was almost too soft and fluffy, mom said its the best she ever had... [coming from asian parent who is kinda picky with their choices, lol]. Overall I think we found our spot and will be a frequent goer from now on. Mind you, the waiting time could be too bizarre but if you were just a small party of 4 or less, it isnt so bad. I give it a solid 4, prices are on point, generous portions, we ordered too many for the two of us but the whole thing could feed 3, I know hahaha.

I have eaten here many times and it by far the most delicious dim sum. I am unclear of the low star rating. The restaurant's dim sum is always on point and meets my expectations. On the weekends, this place is packed and a mad house since it does have a parking lot and by the Asian supermarket. 

If you wanted to avoid the main st flushing area entirely and have some dim sum - this place is a good spot

Just had dim sum there yesterday very consistent we ordered seven dishes of the golden shrimp rice crepes they were delicious along side other staples har gow and siu Mei we ordered a lobster noodle cause we had 14 people in a private room excellent time. My grandkids enjoyed it immensely

Solid dim sum place! My friends and I came as soon as they opened on Memorial Day and there was no wait. We parked on a nearby street pretty easily (yay free holiday parking). The space is massive, nicely decorated--we were sat by a window so it was nicely lit. Food was delicious and tasty! We had a variety of dishes--all were solid. My favorites were the rice roll with crispy shrimp and the sesame rice roll dessert. Both are ones I've never seen before at other dim sum places and they were super unique! I also loved the sweet tofu with a ginger syrup (it was also great the next day as breakfast). The carts don't come around super often but everything was fresh. Would definitely recommend and I agree with others, it's much better than the 3/5 rating.

My first time eating here.  This dim sum restaurant is very large and nicely decorated.  The service was ok as well.
They offer a wide variety of steamed and fried dim sum, as well as Peking duck, king crab, spare ribs, chicken feet, tripe and more. Plenty of vegetarian dishes: tofu, mixed vegetables, assorted stir fry, noodles and fried rice.
They have valet parking here, so if you drive this is the place to go.

It's been a while since last time I had Dim sum in Flushing. I wanted to try a new restaurant so we came here. We went early so no waiting was needed. The food was ok, some of them were cold. The service was ok as well. The price is a bit higher than other dim sum place.

Came for dim sum with my family on a Saturday at around 10:30 in the morning to try and beat the rush. I've been here a few times before for dim sum and birthday dinners but it was years ago. They have street metered parking (not much) or valet parking. The lot looked pretty crowded already but the restaurant still had seats. We had the classic dim sum staples (shrimp/beef churng fun, ha gow, shumai, pork ribs, chicken feet, taro puffs, sticky rice, tripe, meatballs, and fish balls). They were all pretty standard except the pork ribs, which had leftover pork taste so you're better off skipping that one. We also ordered beef chow fun and young chow fried rice. The chow fun was good, but I always love a chow fun. 

We were seated on the platform area, so it was easy to be overlooked (i.e. in getting dim sum, flagging a waiter for water, the bill, etc.). Overall, it was your typical dim sum/Chinese restaurant experience - being ignored by waiters, and dishes that are hit or miss. But it definitely beats going into the heart of Flushing and having to fight for a spot (both parking and a table) there.

Tip - there's a weekday special where you can get medium and large dim sum plates for the price of a small plate.
I a little bit of a madhouse getting seated, but this might be my new dim sum spot.   Everything I had was pretty good.  They also have valet parking.

We had a big gathering here after a funeral.  We appreciated having the private room which was perfect and comfortable for what we needed.  Service was efficient, attentive and fast.  Our traditional banquet style meal was very well prepared with a good variety of options and the food came out quickly with very generous portions.

Only ever ordered takeout. They are consistently fresh, tasty and fast! Every time my family has a craving for dim sum, we always order a big order from here. They have the traditional offerings plus a few a typical HONG KONG restaurant would offer. (Sadly, not many do in NYC) I never had a bad order from them.

After seeing this on Youtube with Lucas Sin, I wanted to try it. Since I was planning a day in Flushing, I knew I had to stop by. The cart ladies were super nice and surprised when my table spoke in Cantonese to them. I think there are better dim sum places in Brooklyn. I was expecting better dishes. I think even the staples such as the chicken feet, har gao, and siu mai were somewhat lackluster. The prices seem a little steeper than in Brooklyn Chinatown as well, but we did get durian puffs which tend to be more expensive.

So unbelievably rude. The ladies at the take out dim sum area are just yelling at customers the whole time. There is no set line, it is unorganized and chaotic. Do not come here unless you're prepared for a screaming match with them just to get your order in and prepare for a lot of bad attitude.
My experience was very good. Dim sum was tasty and fresh. Not sitting on the steamer to long. Service was attentive. Cleanliness was good as well.

Just updating since I came here today with my family for lunch. It was so crowded that I was worried that I made a mistake coming when I couldn't even get anyone to get a number from but when I finally got his attention the gentleman told me it will be quick, 15 minutes. So we waited.
And he was right we were seated in 15 minutes. There was pretty good turnover which is what you want at a dim sum restaurant. It means the food is fresh. The inside is big with many tables as well as side rooms.
Immediately we ordered tea, some noodles, and grabbed some dim sum from the cart going around. I asked them not to put bean sprouts into the beef flat noodles and they obliged. 
The food is still solid. The noodles were cooked well. The beef flat noodles might have under seasoned but the pan fried noodles were nice and crispy. As for the dim sum we didn't order that many: the chicken feet, the turnip cake, fried taro dumpling, and the coconut jelly. They were all solid but the best was the coconut jelly. It was jiggly and the texture was perfect. 
I'm glad this place is still good.

Food was good, little oily/greasy, but the service sucked. Us an 2 other tables, but we have to get up and ask for everything including the check.

The only time they looked busy was when we gave them a small tip and they harassed us over $2
One of the better dim sum places I've been to! The egg tart and steam rice roll were incredible. We came Sunday morning (10am) and got a table immediately. They have valet parking so it's convenient.

Very perfect place for dimsum and dinner. 
Dimsum all the standard small bows items, delicious! Dinner we order swimming fish in soup and chef recommend dishes. All food has been yummy, fresh, good prices. Staff are also very helpful. High recommended. If you don't want to deal with people, just order everything to go, there is a section for u to buy bbq pork chicken duck togo.

The chashu buns this time were perfectly satisfying so I think there is a bit of discrepancy. The eggplant shrimp was cold sadly but wouldve been good if it was hot. The slightly crispy breaded shrimp on cheung fun was still my favorite. This is the best dim sum place in flushing. The egg tarts were out of this world and perfectly buttery, crispy, and hot. Get some to go!

My go to dim sum place. Has reliable and consistent food. It's super crowded on weekends, holidays and Mother's Day but if you go early (or late), you won't need to wait as long. Parking is tough since the tiny parking lot can get full quickly but if you're willing to walk, you can do street parking a couple blocks away. Service is okay as long as you catch the attention of a waiter. Ambience is a typical chinese restaurant...loud!

Last week, together with my family and nephew from Seattle @fromgenesis , we were transported to Hong Kong as we enjoyed dimsum brunch in a huge and bustling dining hall in Flushing, Queens. Just when the big and popular ones in NYC closed shop (Ping's in Queens) or moved to a smaller space (Jing Fong in Manhattan) during and after the pandemic, Lake Pavilion is a survivor -- for a good and delicious reason. Its affordable and quick assortment of freshly made Cantonese treats pushed by friendly non-English speaking ladies in steaming dimsum carts are such a delight in the weekend.Rookie foodie mistake -- dimsum for dinner. For the best dimsum cart experience, come from morning opening to lunch on the weekends. On those busy weekends, it's definitely worth a trip to Flushing.#curious_eater #dimsumtime #flushing queens #queenseats #cantonesefood #dimsumcart #dimsumbreakfast
I thought the food was overall much better this time. I was pretty happy with my choices. This is my first time trying the salted egg yolk buns, a tad on the sweet side, but still delicious!

This should be "0" star review. Anyone noticed dim sum workers have been very aggressive in sales nowadays ? One particular woman in take out section here was outright sneaky. We picked up some dim sum takeouts for some family members who did not join us for the gathering. Among many items we bought, we asked for 2 dishes of chaozhou dumplings. There was one available in the counter and she offered another kind. We declined and so she went inside the dining hall to check if any pushing cart has any. That sounded like a nice person but she actually brought out taro dumplings (which looked similar from distance). Not more dining here ever again.

Wanted to try this dim sum spot because I heard it's the best in Queens. It's a large restaurant kind of nicely decorated with very traditional Chinese decor. There are dim sum carts going around even on weekdays which makes it a very lively ambiance.

Service was very good: the dim sum ladies were extremely helpful in locating the items we asked for. Tea was filling promptly and empty plates were taken away constantly.

We had a variety of dishes: shrimp dumplings, pork dumplings (siu mai), beef rice rolls, fried shrimp rice rolls, bean curd skin rolls, veal chops with black been sauce, pan fried chive & shrimp dumplings, BBQ pork pineapple buns, Cantonese sponge cake, and egg tarts. Everything was solid; the standouts being the fried shrimp rice rolls, the shrimp dumplings, the BBQ pork pineapple buns, the pan fried chive & shrimp dumplings, and the egg tarts.

Prices were very affordable. On weekdays, the small, medium, and large items are all charged as small which is $4.25. The really excellent egg tarts and BBQ pork pineapple buns are among these $4.25 dishes which I thought were absolute steals! 

One star was taken off because I did feel a bit thirsty afterwards. It would have been perfect if they would have gone a bit easier on the msg. Other than that it was a really delicious and delightful dim sum experience.

Party of 3 came for dinner, they rushed us to table, then had to wait 10 minutes for menus, then 10 minutes for waiter to take the order . 3 dishes. 2 other tables of 4 or more came in after us and got food before us, 20 minutes till ouour food arrived. Could be racism as I am white but husband and MIL are chinese.Chinese. eggplant with braised beef ribs was more like eggplant with ribs no meat. Crispy pork chops (sweet and sour) was mostly breading and very fatty. The crispy noodles with beef was ok. No red bean soup, just orange slices. They used to be better, not sure what happened

My friends and I went here for Sunday Dim Sum service. Food was superb! Very glad that we have friends who speaks Chinese (I'm assuming Cantonese) who were able to order for us. Especially the Chicken pan fried noodles which was a special dish (it wasn't in the carts)

They only serve Dim Sum 9 AM to 3 PM. I got there around 12:15 pm. Thanked that some of our peeps got there by 11:30 am to secure a Table.

The restaurant is 15 mins bus ride from downtown Flushing, Area. If you want an authentic Chinese food taste and affordable, this IS the place to be ‍

I enjoy the dim sum 
They are open on Sunday 
The foods are always good 
They are excellent!

Dim sum!  This place seems to be always super packed on weekends around noon time.  Everyone is packed in like sardines, waiting around for a table, by the front cashier area.  Just get a number from the bald guy wearing a tie, shouting out numbers and frantically waving his hands around a lot. 

Decor:  Lots of nice big tables.  Standard decor for these types of places.  Nothing new in the way of design.  

On to the food.  Ordered a variety of dim sum.  Unfortunately Nothing stood out and I actually didn't like anything.  Felt like everything was substandard.  A lot of it seemed to be boiled to heat it up and save time and kitchen space.  This makes food rather tasteless.

Kudos for the massive selection of dim sum items to choose from.  Many types other places do not make.  Some of the elders at the table enjoyed super OG steamed rice balls with meat filling that were decorated with a leaf held with a toothpick.  Not my thing.  Personally I'd prefer a smaller variety of dishes that are better made.

Chow mein noodles came to the table, burnt black around the outer edges of the noodle dish.

Shao mai was doughy with giant chunks of fat.  Tofu fa was very tasteless and watery.  Radish cakes barely had any radish flavor.  Eggplant w shrimp were huge, but seemed like mostly fat.  No one wanted to finish them.  Tried a lot of other dim sum too but don't really wanna go on, on how mediocre it was.

Lots of push carts filled with dim sum being rolled around everywhere.  Though I think not all of them made it into the back of the restaurant where we were sitting.  Or were just sold out before reaching the back.

Service was great.  Tea was refilled immediately, plates were removed efficiently, and even asked if we wanted fresh plates.

I won't go back, considering there is so much competition.  Lots of other places to choose from.

BLUF: Competent dinner service; dim-sum seekers should go elsewhere.

Lake Pavilion is a main draw due to its location outside of Downtown Flushing and close proximity to the Long Island Expressway. The restaurant's parking lot and hallways are tightly filled during peak brunch hours on the weekends.

Dinner service is good. Lake Pavilion offers a huge menu, and it feels like the chefs know how to make everything on it well.

The dim-sum suffers from hurried, volume production. For example, the chicken feet seemed to have been reheated in a pot of boiling water, instead of being steamed. We've also noticed some dishes (like siu mai) are consistently fattier than other places, and that sometimes trays of food (like the crispy taro puffs) are freshly served lukewarm instead of hot.

Service is consistently good for both dim-sum and dinner.

Good portions, no flavor and very bad service
I was waiting to try this restaurant because the outdoor decoration is so welcoming but was a bad experience, the waitress server our food and never come back to ask if we need something else or check if everything is ok; btw it was not, we ask to other waiter for more sauce and he brought a tiny tiny cup of sauce and again never come back so if you like a good service this is not the place you wanna try.

Lamb chops were good, the appetizer of scallops, shrimps and squid so so and the Seafood pineapple fried rice was so simple, no flavor and "seafood" = baby shrimps chopped in small pieces so the food also was mediocre and no recommended.

I asked for a bottle of wine and the waitress didn't know nothing about what kind of wine can offer us so in the end I asked for a glass of wine of the house and beer because we didn't have option meanwhile in the entrance there is an extensive bar, so on the drinks the experience was bad too.

We went to New Lake for dim sum, arrived around 10:45am, parking and restaurant was so busy! There is parking right behind the restaurant and they are very well managed. We were able to get a table quickly, however we had to share. They asked if we wanted to wait for a private small table or get seated immediately but we had to share the table. We opted to get seated immediately and shared our table in the main dining area. The dining room is large, and note there are also many small private rooms which also had full tables.

There are many dim sum ladies pushing their carts, with one of the largest varieties! We ordered many dishes, such as har gow, stuffed eggplant, durian puff, durian mochi, shrimp rice rolls, egg tart, and so many more! I felt the pace of the carts were well timed, they did not rush over when you sat down, there was always a constant flow of fresh dim sum options. 

I had the best egg tart here, it was so warm, flaky and perfect! And hubby loved the durian mochi. Overall, we are definitely making this our go-to dim sum spot going forward! Definitely a hidden gem away from the busy Flushing Main street.
Food so tasty. Great dim sum spot, classic vibe and easy parking. Would highly recommend it here

It's been awhile since my last visit to this restaurant. I was surprised to find out the insane price for just 6 little fried dumplings which cost over $10. Another Cantonese restaurant which 2 blocks down cost $7.59. And taste better.  Well I've learned my lesson. Not coming to this place anymore.

New Lake Pavilion in Flushing is a fantastic spot for a breakfast feast, especially if you love dim sum. I ordered about nine dishes, and each one was well-prepared and flavorful. The highlights were the shrimp dumplings and barbecue pork buns--both fresh and perfectly balanced. The congee was comforting, and the fried taro puffs had a great texture. Everything arrived quickly and piping hot, which made the experience even better.

The ambience is modern and elegant, with spacious seating and plenty of natural light in the morning. Despite being busy, the space felt calm and organized.

Service was efficient and attentive. The staff were quick to take orders, refill tea, and clear plates without making you feel rushed.

Overall, New Lake Pavilion delivers on food, ambience, and service--a solid choice for a hearty breakfast in Flushing. I'll definitely be back to explore more of their menu!

Family comes here for dim sum once in awhile. Busy on weekends like a lot of dim sum places, good food, kids like it, parking lot available along with street parking. Want to go to dinner there one day but have not yet. Service is great

We came here for dinner since our kids home from college were craving good Chinese food. It didn't disappoint. The dishes were good portion size. We ordered the sweet and sour chicken off menu and it was excellent. I liked that it was more chicken than batter. The sautéed pea shoots and sautéed grouper filets were yum. The beef pan fried noodles was huge and we took home the leftovers. Service was efficient. Nice decor and there are private rooms available. There is valet parking in the back of the restaurant. We will return!

This restaurant was pretty good a few years ago and I have always wanted to come back. But life has been busy and I haven't been able to come back here for years, possibly 5 years.

My 3 year old who really love the exterior of the restaurant, after coming home, she threw up.  For the next few days, she would have frequent visits to the bathroom.  Could it be a coincidence?  Perhaps. But I would stay clear of this restaurant until their rating goes up.

Smelled absolutely gross like a dumpster , lo mein tasted like it was from a dollar tree freezer. the service was so bad and the people pushed me and yelled at me just because I accidentally was gonna go through the wrong exit. they slapped the bill  in my face. Don't come here unless you wanna throw up from the weird smell and the unsanitary stained chairs.

This is our go to for dimsum.

Good food, not in the crazy flushing downtown area and plenty of seating =  less wait time. We come here for both dine in and take out. Prices are good for the quality.

The place can use some glam up but it's good enough. The push cart servers are typical in terms of service (not super easy friendly but answers questions when asked).

This place gets really busy and rightfully so.  They have all the typical dimsum and special, limited dishes on Sunday that I don't see during the week.  Always pick the dimsum from underneath so it's freshest!
Always an enjoyable time here with family. Friendly and attentive staff and food is always on point and hot. Definitely one of my go to places. The decor is very well designed and welcoming.

Awesome dim sum place featured on Bon appetit's Eat everything on the menu segment. My favourites are the buns and anything with shrimp

This place is a solid choice for dim sum. They offer a large variety of the classic dishes such as steamed dumplings, shumai, bao buns, rice rolls, etc to name a few.

The service is efficient and it's a good spot if you're dining with a group. The atmosphere is lively but comfortable, exactly what you'd expect from a quintessential dim sum place.

Overall, if you're in the mood for traditional dim sum, this place delivers good food at a fair price. Definitely worth checking out.

Everything was so bad. I would never go back to this place. It was all bad. The food is soggy and cold. I really don't like dim sum. This place was highly recommended so I tried to go there with an open mind but no! Just no

Solid dimsum spot with all of the rolling the carts! The ladies running there carts are mildly aggressive to offer you all the goodies from their carts, but don't be shy to just choose the dishes you like or ask where you can get the dishes you wanna try! My friends and I visited on a rainy Saturday morning to do a belated Lunar new year celebration here this year. Get the fried shrimp roll wrapped in cheung fun (we collectively loved this one), spare ribs (they lay it in a bed of tiny cheung fun!!) , siu mai (they make it with a huge piece of shrimp on top!), if you can! Tried the other dim sum classics too (chicken feet, ha gow, tripe, salted egg yolk buns, bean curd rolls, fried taro), which were good and def fills that craving. Lovely family spot! Valet parking available but looked like it filled up quick. Good amount of street parking nearby though! Would 10/10 come back

Great traditional dim sum, nostalgic push carts and delicious steamed aroma as each cart passes your table. A Sunday ritual for my family and I. Recommend coming early since it does fill up quickly and there is parking outside behind the restaurant and street parking. Servers were attentive and refilled our tea whenever we ran low. Definitely our to go spot in queens for dim sum !

New Lake Pavillion, please always be in business!!
This is my go-to spot for dim sum! I was first introduced to this location by my in-laws 10 years ago and I have been coming back ever since. 
There are a few parking spaces at the front of the restaurant which is almost never available. There is also a pay-what-you-want valet parking at the back of the restaurant. The attendants are so helpful!

The way can vary between 10-30 minutes. For large parties, I suggest calling ahead or arrive early enough to beat the crowd. Dim sum is considered breakfast so expect a crowd on those times.

I love the assortment of dishes they serve. What's better is that they rotate in carts which is the traditional serving style, I am told. Even if you have to order from a server, that doesn't take away from the deliciousness of each piece.

For every visit, we always have to have the egg custard bun. If you happen to see it, grab it! You won't know when you'll see it again. It goes so quick. There had been times I had to ask a server for it because it's gone as soon as it comes out.

Thank you for an always appetizing meal!
